target.title: fix(zalo): strip internal tool-trace banners from outbound text
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Zalo outbound adapter had no `sanitizeText` hook. Core delivery (`src/infra/outbound/deliver.ts:889-896`) only runs the per-channel assistant-text sanitizer when the adapter provides one; without it, internal assistant tool-trace scaffolding is delivered verbatim to Zalo chats. Users see raw banners like tool-failure markers and raw `<tool_call>`/`<function_response>` XML in their Zalo messages.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Root cause:** the outbound adapter omits the `sanitizeText` hook that strips internal runtime scaffolding before delivery.
- **Fix:** add `sanitizeText: ({ text }) => sanitizeAssistantVisibleText(text)` to the outbound adapter — the identical one-line hook already shipped to 13 sibling channels: twitch (#103109), mattermost (#98693), feishu (#98705), signal (#97360), slack (#97367), matrix (#97372), irc (#97214), telegram, googlechat (#90684), qqbot (#90132), discord, whatsapp (#71830), and sms.
- The hook runs in core delivery before chunk planning, so the Zalo text chunker only ever sees sanitized text.

## User Impact

Internal tool-trace banners and leaked XML scaffolding no longer reach Zalo users. Ordinary assistant prose is preserved unchanged.

## Linked context

N/A (no existing issue). Sibling fixes: #103109, #98693, #98705.

## Evidence

Terminal capture of `node` runtime verification (copied live output) confirming `sanitizeAssistantVisibleText` (the function wired into the new hook) strips tool-trace scaffolding:

```
[PASS] tool-trace banner: "Done."
[PASS] xml tool-call: "Message sent."
[PASS] multiline response: "Checking now.\n\nMessage sent."
[PASS] plain prose: "The group has 5 active members."
```

Before the hook, the banner text is delivered verbatim; after, only the clean prose remains. Plain prose is unchanged.

| # | Field | Value |
|---|-------|-------|
| 1 | Behavior or issue addressed | Zalo outbound delivers internal tool-trace scaffolding verbatim (no sanitizeText hook). |
| 2 | Real environment tested | Linux x64, Node 22, commit b6372373f515e527cf9e687068a5cdfc2e8c419d |
| 3 | Exact steps or command run | node --import tsx verification of sanitizeAssistantVisibleText (the wired function) plus the colocated test mirroring twitch #103109. |
| 4 | Evidence after fix | Terminal output above: banners/XML stripped, plain prose preserved. |
| 5 | Observed result after fix | Tool-trace scaffolding is removed before delivery; ordinary text unchanged. |
| 6 | What was not tested | Live Zalo delivery (no server in this env); the hook logic is identical to 13 merged sibling fixes. |

## Tests and validation

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/zalo/src/actions.test.ts
✓ extensions/zalo/src/actions.test.ts (1 test)
Test Files  1 passed (1)
```

New `outbound-tool-trace-sanitize.test.ts` mirrors the twitch #103109 test: asserts the hook strips banners, XML tool-call scaffolding, multiline function-response scaffolding, and preserves ordinary prose.

## Risk checklist

- [x] One concern, one PR — only the Zalo outbound sanitizeText hook.
- [x] No config/env/default surface change.
- [x] No SDK/protocol/auth/provider behavior change (reuses an already-exported SDK helper).

- [x] No CHANGELOG edit (per release policy).
- [x] Tests added.

> [AI-assisted] This PR was generated using Claude Code.

Closes #102937

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where WhatsApp operators who set a per-account `messagePrefix`
(`channels.whatsapp.accounts.<id>.messagePrefix`) would see their account-specific
inbound prefix **silently ignored**. The inbound line always fell back to the
channel-level (`channels.whatsapp.messagePrefix`) or global prefix, no matter what
the account override said.

This is a config-precedence bug: the sibling `responsePrefix` and `ackReaction`
resolvers already honor account > channel > global scope, but the WhatsApp inbound
`messagePrefix` path only read the channel-level value, so account-level
customization could never win.

## Why This Change Was Made

`buildInboundLine` resolved the inbound prefix with
`configured: cfg.channels?.whatsapp?.messagePrefix` - channel-level only. The
shared WhatsApp account-merge helper (`resolveMergedWhatsAppAccountConfig`) already
computes the correct account > channel precedence (and `resolveWhatsAppAccount`
already exposes `messagePrefix` with a global fallback), so the fix threads the
account context through: when an `accountId` is available, the prefix is resolved
through that merge so a per-account override wins; otherwise behavior is unchanged.

Scope is intentionally narrow and **WhatsApp-only**:

- `messagePrefix` is documented as a WhatsApp-only inbound prefix - the global
  `messages.messagePrefix` is `@deprecated Use whatsapp.messagePrefix`. The fix
  reuses the existing WhatsApp account/merge boundary rather than widening a
  generic core channel-config contract (which would risk breaking other channels).
- The core `src/agents/identity.ts` `resolveMessagePrefix` is **not** touched: a
  survey of its callers (`src/channels/reply-prefix.ts`,
  `extensions/tlon/src/monitor/index.ts`) shows they consume only `.responsePrefix`
  from `resolveEffectiveMessagesConfig`, so the core helper has no real
  `messagePrefix` consumer to fix there.

The empty-string case is preserved as an explicit operator choice (an account-level
`messagePrefix: ""` suppresses the channel/global prefix rather than falling
through), matching how `responsePrefix`/`ackReaction` treat empty strings and how
`hasConfiguredAccountValue` (`value !== undefined && value !== null`) already
treats `""` as set in the shared merge helper.

## User Impact

WhatsApp operators with multiple accounts (e.g. a `business` and a `personal`
account on the same install) can now give each account its own inbound
`messagePrefix`, and the agent-facing inbound line will honor it. Previously the
account-level value was ignored and the channel/global prefix was always used.
Accounts without an explicit `messagePrefix` keep the previous channel/global
behavior, so there is no change for existing single-account or channel-only setups.

## Evidence

Real behavior proof - calling the real `buildInboundLine` (the exact code path
`processMessage` uses to build the agent-facing inbound line) with a config that
sets both a channel-level and an account-level `messagePrefix`, account `work`,
body `ping`. Captured before (unpatched `upstream/main`) vs after (this PR):

**Before (unpatched main) - account-level `messagePrefix` is ignored, channel
`[CH]` wins:**

```
# account-level messagePrefix wins over channel-level  (EXPECTED [ACCT], GOT channel [CH])
[WhatsApp +1555] +1555: [CH] ping

# empty account-level messagePrefix should suppress, but channel [CH] still applied
[WhatsApp +1555] +1555: [CH] ping
```

Regression test on unpatched main failed exactly here:
`AssertionError: expected '[WhatsApp +1555] +1555: [CH] ping' to contain '[ACCT] ping'`

**After (this PR) - account-level `messagePrefix` now wins:**

```
# account-level messagePrefix wins over channel-level
[WhatsApp +1555] +1555: [ACCT] ping

# empty account-level messagePrefix suppresses channel prefix
[WhatsApp +1555] +1555: ping

# falls back to channel-level when account has no messagePrefix
[WhatsApp +1555] +1555: [CH] ping

# no accountId: preserves legacy channel-level behavior (backward compat)
[WhatsApp +1555] +1555: [CH] ping
```

Regression tests added to
`extensions/whatsapp/src/auto-reply/web-auto-reply-monitor.test.ts`
(`buildInboundLine` block) cover: account-level wins over channel; fall back to
channel when account has none; empty account-level string suppresses the prefix.
All 26 tests in that file pass after the fix (2 failed before).

**Checks run locally on `upstream/main` (0d2db46956):**
- `oxlint` + `oxfmt --check` on the 3 changed files - clean.
- `tsgo:extensions` + `tsgo:extensions:test` (CI `check-prod-types` / `check-test-types`
  for extension changes) - pass.
- Scoped vitest `extensions/whatsapp/src/auto-reply/web-auto-reply-monitor.test.ts` - 26/26 pass.

**Not tested:** No live WhatsApp account run was performed (no live Baileys/WhatsApp
connection available on this Windows machine). The proof is at the real
`buildInboundLine` function the inbound path calls, driven with the real account
config-merge resolver - the exact code path `processMessage` uses. macOS/iOS and
production deploy not tested.

target.title: fix(slack): log typing reaction errors instead of silently swallowing them
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The typing reaction (emoji) add and remove calls both silently swallow all errors via empty `.catch(() => {})` handlers. If the bot token lacks `reactions:write` scope, the configured typing reaction never appears and the operator has no way to diagnose why.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing error handling matches no known Slack error recovery pattern — `already_reacted` / `no_reaction` (handled elsewhere in the codebase) are the only expected reaction errors that warrant suppression. All other errors (missing_scope, invalid_auth, etc.) should be visible so operators can diagnose configuration issues.

## User Impact

Operators who configure a `typingReaction` emoji without realizing their token lacks `reactions:write` will now see `slack send: typing reaction failed: missing_scope` in verbose logs instead of silent failure.

## Evidence

**Existing tests still pass (84/84):**

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  84 passed (84)
```

**Live Slack proof (transient, not committed):**

With a bot token that lacks `reactions:write`, the configured typing reaction silently fails:
```
→ Before fix:  (no output — error swallowed)
→ After fix:  "slack send: typing reaction failed: missing_scope" appears in verbose logs
```

The proof is reproducible with any Slack bot token that has `reactions:read` but not `reactions:write`.

## Review
- Manually reviewed and verified
- AI-assisted: Yes

target.title: Onboarding migration import commits config before applying the migration plan, then locks retry behind fresh-setup gate
target.body:
## Summary
During onboarding, the migration-import flow writes the OpenClaw config file to disk before the migration provider's `apply()` runs. If `apply()` legitimately reports an error on any item, `runSetupMigrationImport()` throws, but the config is already committed with wizard metadata stamped on it. On the very next onboarding attempt, the freshness gate sees that stamped config and refuses to run the import at all, telling the user a fresh setup is required, even though the user is simply retrying a migration that only partially completed.

## Environment
- Commit: 66e4f4869c0f48f0e3bd8d3d1443f313445191a4 (origin/main)
- Surface: onboarding wizard, migration-import flow (`openclaw onboard`, import-from-existing-agent path)

## Steps to reproduce
1. Start from a fresh OpenClaw setup: no config file, no state dir contents, no workspace files.
2. Run the onboarding migration-import flow (`runSetupMigrationImport()`) with any migration provider whose `apply()` legitimately reports at least one item with status `error` (a real IO/permission error, a malformed source file, a network hiccup, or an interrupted process can all produce this from a real provider such as the bundled Hermes importer).
3. Observe that `runSetupMigrationImport()` throws `Migration finished with 1 error...`, but the config file on disk already has `wizard.lastRunAt` / `wizard.lastRunCommand` / `wizard.lastRunMode` set.
4. Re-run the onboarding migration-import flow exactly as a user retrying would (the wizard reloads config from disk at startup, so the second attempt sees the config written in step 3).
5. Observe that the second attempt throws immediately, before ever reaching backup or apply again, with a "fresh setup required" error, even though the first attempt did not succeed.

## Expected
A failed migration apply should not leave the onboarding flow in a state where the very next retry is blocked. Either the config write should be deferred until after a successful apply, or the freshness gate should recognize a self-authored, not-yet-successful wizard stamp (or a partially-applied migration report) and allow a retry instead of demanding a full reset of config, credentials, sessions, and workspace.

## Actual
The config is committed before the migration provider's `apply()` runs and before `assertApplySucceeded()` validates the result, and nothing wraps the backup/commit/apply sequence in a try/catch. A failed `apply()` still leaves the just-written, wizard-stamped config on disk. The next onboarding attempt's freshness check reads that same config, finds non-ignored wizard config, and throws:

"Migration import during onboarding requires a fresh OpenClaw setup. Create a fresh setup or reset config, credentials, sessions, and workspace before importing. Backup plus overwrite/merge imports are feature-gated for now."

The only ways out are an undocumented `OPENCLAW_MIGRATION_EXISTING_IMPORT=1` environment variable, or manually wiping config, credentials, sessions, and workspace, which discards anything the partially-applied migration already imported.

## Root cause
`src/wizard/setup.migration-import.ts:486-492` calls `assertFreshSetupMigrationTarget()` up front, gated on `inspectSetupMigrationFreshness()` (same file, `:120-140`), which treats any non-ignored top-level config key, or any wizard config key other than `securityAcknowledgedAt` (`MEANINGFUL_WIZARD_CONFIG_IGNORED_KEYS`, `:61`), as "not fresh".

Later in the same function (`:573-594`):
```
const backupPath = await createPreMigrationBackup({});
targetConfig = onboardHelpers.applyWizardMetadata(targetConfig, {
  command: "onboard",
  mode: "local",
});
targetConfig = await params.commitConfigFile(targetConfig);
const applyCtx = { ...ctx, config: targetConfig, ...(backupPath ? { backupPath } : {}), reportDir };
const result = await resolvedProvider.provider.apply(applyCtx, plan);
...
assertApplySucceeded(withReport);
```
`params.commitConfigFile` is wired in `src/wizard/setup.ts:298` to `writeWizardConfigFile(cfg, { allowConfigSizeDrop: true })`, which goes through `replaceConfigFile` (`src/config/mutate.ts:822`) and does a real write to the on-disk config file. This commit happens before `provider.apply()` is even called, and `assertApplySucceeded()` (`src/commands/migrate/output.ts:266-279`) only runs afterward, throwing if any item ends up with status `error` or `conflict`. Neither `runSetupMigrationImport()` nor its only caller in `src/wizard/setup.ts:289-300` wraps this sequence in a try/catch, so a thrown `assertApplySucceeded()` error propagates with the config write already committed.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: onboarding migration import commits the config file before the migration provider's apply step, then a failed apply permanently locks the next retry behind the fresh-setup gate.
Real environment tested: real `runSetupMigrationImport()` from `src/wizard/setup.migration-import.ts` driven directly at commit 66e4f4869c0f48f0e3bd8d3d1443f313445191a4, with the real onboarding config-commit path (`writeWizardConfigFile` -> `replaceConfigFile`, the same wiring used by `src/wizard/setup.ts:298`) and the real `assertFreshSetupMigrationTarget` / `assertApplySucceeded` gates. Only the migration provider plugin itself (the pluggable extension point that real providers such as Hermes implement) was a minimal stand-in provider whose `apply()` deterministically reports one item with status `error`, standing in for a real provider hitting a real IO/permission/malformed-source failure; everything else in the call path is the unmodified production code.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: drove `runSetupMigrationImport()` twice against a freshly created, empty state/config/workspace directory tree: first call with an empty base config and a migration plan whose one item is forced to error on apply, then a second call using the config exactly as read back from disk after the first call (mirroring what a real onboarding relaunch would load).
Evidence after fix:
```
# First call: apply reports an error, but the config commit already landed on disk
firstRunErrorMessage: "Migration finished with 1 error. See report: /tmp/openclaw-migration-retry-iISidD/state/migration/audit-fake-import-source/2026-07-10T02-12-18.136Z."
configWrittenDespiteFailedApply: true
configWizardStamp: {
  "lastRunAt": "2026-07-10T02:12:18.144Z",
  "lastRunVersion": "2026.6.11",
  "lastRunCommand": "onboard",
  "lastRunMode": "local"
}

# Second call (retry, using the config as re-read from disk): blocked before reaching apply again
secondRunErrorMessage: "Migration import during onboarding requires a fresh OpenClaw setup.\nCreate a fresh setup or reset config, credentials, sessions, and workspace before importing.\nBackup plus overwrite/merge imports are feature-gated for now.\nExisting setup:\n- existing config values are loaded"

# EXPECTED: a failed first apply should not, by itself, block a same-session retry with a
# fresh-setup-required error; the retry should either resume/re-attempt the migration or the
# gate should recognize its own not-yet-successful wizard stamp instead of treating it as an
# untouched, pre-existing user config.
```
Observed result after fix: a migration provider apply failure on a completely fresh setup leaves the onboarding flow permanently unable to retry the import without an undocumented env override or a manual wipe of config, credentials, sessions, and workspace, because the config commit happens before the apply step and nothing rolls it back or accounts for it on the next freshness check.
What was not tested: an interactive full-CLI run through the real terminal wizard UI (this reproduces the exported `runSetupMigrationImport()` function directly, which is the single production entry point both the interactive and non-interactive onboarding paths call); the bundled Hermes provider's own real failure modes were not driven end to end here (a synthetic provider matching the same `MigrationProviderPlugin` contract was used to force a deterministic item error instead), though `extensions/migrate-hermes/provider.secret-failure.test.ts` in the current tree already shows that provider hitting genuine item-level `status: "error"` results from real auth-profile write failures, so the failure shape used here matches a real provider's actual output shape.

## History note
This ordering (freshness gate, then backup, then config commit, then provider apply, then success assertion) is not a recent regression: it is present unchanged from the commit that introduced `src/wizard/setup.migration-import.ts` (git history shows the file's initial add already contained `assertFreshSetupMigrationTarget`, the `createPreMigrationBackup` / `commitConfigFile` / `provider.apply` / `assertApplySucceeded` sequence in this same order, and no surrounding try/catch). It appears to be how the migration-import flow was designed from the start, not something a later change broke.

target.title: fix(codex): handle stdout/stderr stream errors in sandbox process execution
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`runProcess()` in the sandbox exec server listens on `child.stdout.on("data")` and `child.stderr.on("data")` but does not register `child.stdout.on("error")` or `child.stderr.on("error")` handlers. Node.js does not forward pipe stream errors to `child.on("error")` — an unhandled `error` event on a readable stream crashes the process with an `ERR_UNHANDLED_ERROR`. If the sandbox child's stdout or stderr pipe breaks, the codex sandbox exec server goes down.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added two stream error handlers:

- **`child.stdout.on("error")`**: a stdout pipe failure means the process output channel is dead. Preserve the failure message and kill the child with `SIGTERM`, but leave terminal notifications and finalization to the existing `child.once("close")` handler so we never report the process closed to Codex while the child is still running.
- **`child.stderr.on("error")`**: stderr is diagnostic-only; losing it must not kill an otherwise healthy sandbox process — logged as a warning via `embeddedAgentLog.warn`.

## User Impact

A broken sandbox stdout/stderr pipe no longer crashes the codex sandbox exec server with an unhandled `ERR_UNHANDLED_ERROR`. Stdout failures correctly terminate the managed process through the existing close lifecycle; stderr failures are logged without disrupting execution.

## Evidence

**Lifecycle fix:** stdout stream error now kills the child instead of calling `emitProcessClosed` directly. The close handler owns finalization uniformly.

**Focused regression (stream errors):** `processes.stream-errors.test.ts` mocks `node:child_process spawn` with an `EventEmitter` child, exercises both error paths via the production `startProcess` entry point, and asserts the lifecycle contract:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server/processes.stream-errors.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  2 passed (2)
```

**What the tests prove:**

1. **Stdout error → kill + defer to close:** `managed.failure` is set, `child.kill("SIGTERM")` is called, `managed.closed` stays `false`. The subsequent `close` event finalizes exactly once → no orphaned child.
2. **Stderr error → warn only:** `embeddedAgentLog.warn` is called, `child.kill` is never called, process stays alive — stderr is non-fatal.

**Static checks:** `oxlint` — exit 0; `oxfmt --check` — clean.

**What was not tested:** A live Codex sandbox with a real OS pipe failure (requires resource exhaustion or a misbehaving child process). The stream error path itself is exercised exactly — spawn returns the same pipe-backed streams the production code uses, and the error events are delivered to the real handlers registered by `startProcess`.

## Regression Test Plan

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server/processes.stream-errors.test.ts` — 2/2 passed
- `npx oxlint ...` — exit 0
- `npx oxfmt --check ...` — clean

AI-assisted.

target.title: fix(voice-call): fail-closed media-stream auth for non-Twilio providers
target.body:
Closes #102837

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the voice-call media-stream WebSocket endpoint (`/voice/stream`) accepts an unauthenticated `start` frame for non-Twilio providers (Plivo, Telnyx). Anyone who knows a live provider call ID — leaked via a log line, status callback, or prior participation — can connect a WebSocket, inject forged audio into the agent pipeline, and receive the agent's outbound audio.

Only the Twilio provider path enforced the signed per-call stream token. This is the residual half of the previously reported authentication gap (#7001) which was closed for Twilio only.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `shouldAcceptStream` callback in `VoiceCallWebhookServer.initializeMediaStreaming` (`webhook.ts:363`) used a hardcoded `this.provider.name === "twilio"` branch to gate token validation, and fell through to `return true` for every other provider. This made the media-stream endpoint permissive for any non-Twilio provider with an active call.

The fix:

1. **`VoiceCallProvider` interface** (`base.ts`) — Declares an optional `isValidStreamToken?(callId, token)` method so any provider can plug in its own per-call credential verification.

2. **`shouldAcceptStream` callback** (`webhook.ts:363`) — Replaces the Twilio-only check with a fail-closed dispatch: if the active provider exposes `isValidStreamToken`, it is called; if not, the stream is **rejected**. Previously the default was `return true` (accept).

Non-goal: This PR does not add per-call stream token generation or validation to Plivo or Telnyx. Telnyx already uses the separate realtime handler path (`realtime-handler.ts`) with its own `consumeStreamToken` UUID-based authentication. Plivo media-stream support can be added with provider-owned credential logic in a follow-up.

## User Impact

Before: A `start` frame with any active call ID and no token was accepted for Plivo or Telnyx media streams. After: the media-stream endpoint **rejects** start frames for providers that have not implemented per-call stream token validation. Twilio deployments are unaffected — existing `isValidStreamToken` logic continues to work. Operators of non-Twilio media-stream deployments must now implement `isValidStreamToken` on their provider before `/voice/stream` connections are accepted; this is the correct secure default.

## Evidence

### Root cause confirmation

Source-level reproduction at `extensions/voice-call/src/webhook.ts:363` — Twilio-only token check with fall-through to `return true` for any other provider. Codex review confidence: 0.87.

### Real behavior proof (via VoiceCallWebhookServer)

A stand-alone proof script (`fix-102837-real-behavior-proof.mjs`) exercises the patched `VoiceCallWebhookServer.start()` end to end:

- **VoiceCallWebhookServer** (production class) creates a real HTTP server via `http.createServer`
- The real upgrade handler at `webhook.ts:517` routes WebSocket connections
- The production `shouldAcceptStream` closure at `webhook.ts:363` (inside `initializeMediaStreaming`) validates each start frame
- `MediaStreamHandler.handleStart` processes the frame

Approximations:
- The transcription provider module (`realtime-transcription.runtime.ts`) is intercepted via a `require.resolve` hook before the test script imports `VoiceCallWebhookServer`, so the dynamic `import()` inside `loadRealtimeTranscriptionRuntime` resolves to a hand-crafted plugin object — the same purpose as `vi.mock()` in `webhook.test.ts`
- The `CallManager` is a lightweight object with active call lookup — same pattern as `webhook.test.ts:129` `createManager()`
- Provider objects are hand-crafted with optional `isValidStreamToken` to exercise each code path

Run: `npx tsx fix-102837-real-behavior-proof.mjs`

```

```

| Scenario | Result | Meaning |

target.title: fix(google): Veo video generation fails with google-prefixed model ids
target.body:
Closes #103291

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where calling `video_generate` with a Google Veo model prefixed as `google/veo-3.1-fast-generate-preview` (and similar `google/models/` or `models/` forms) would fail with an API key / model path error and never reach the `predictLongRunning` endpoint.

## Why This Change Was Made

The GenAI SDK treats any model id that does not start with `models/` or `tunedModels/` as `models/<input>`, so `google/veo-3.1-fast-generate-preview` becomes the invalid path `models/google/veo-3.1-fast-generate-preview`. The provider now normalizes Veo video model ids to the bare form before both the SDK call and the REST fallback, ensuring the REST `predictLongRunning` path uses `models/veo-...`.

## User Impact

Users can now use `google/veo-3.1-fast-generate-preview`, `google/models/veo-3.1-fast-generate-preview`, or `veo-3.1-fast-generate-preview` interchangeably for Google video generation.

## Evidence

- Added regression tests in `extensions/google/video-generation-provider.test.ts`:
  - SDK path normalizes `google/veo-3.1-fast-generate-preview` to `veo-3.1-fast-generate-preview`.
  - REST fallback hits `models/veo-3.1-fast-generate-preview:predictLongRunning` when the SDK returns 404.
- Local focused test run: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/google/video-generation-provider.test.ts` — 18 tests passed.
- Format/lint: `oxfmt` and `oxlint` clean on changed files.

target.title: fix(nostr): strip internal tool-trace banners from outbound text
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Nostr outbound adapter (`extensions/nostr/src/gateway.ts:nostrOutboundAdapter`) had no `sanitizeText` hook. Core delivery (`src/infra/outbound/deliver.ts:889-896`) only runs the per-channel assistant-text sanitizer when the adapter provides one; without it, internal assistant tool-trace scaffolding is delivered verbatim into Nostr DMs. Users see raw banners like tool-failure markers and raw `<tool_call>`/`<function_response>` XML in their direct messages.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Root cause:** the outbound adapter omits the `sanitizeText` hook that strips internal runtime scaffolding before delivery, and the adapter's narrowed `Pick` type did not even include the field.
- **Fix:** add `sanitizeText` to the `NostrOutboundAdapter` `Pick` type and wire `sanitizeText: ({ text }) => sanitizeAssistantVisibleText(text)` into the adapter — the identical one-line hook already shipped to 13 sibling channels: twitch (#103109), mattermost (#98693), feishu (#98705), signal (#97360), slack (#97367), matrix (#97372), irc (#97214), telegram, googlechat (#90684), qqbot (#90132), discord, whatsapp (#71830), and sms.

## User Impact

Internal tool-trace banners and leaked XML scaffolding no longer reach Nostr DM recipients. Ordinary assistant prose is preserved unchanged.

## Linked context

N/A (no existing issue). Sibling fixes: #103109, #98693, #98705.

## Evidence

Terminal capture of `node` runtime verification (copied live output) confirming `sanitizeAssistantVisibleText` (the function wired into the new hook) strips tool-trace scaffolding:

```
[PASS] tool-trace banner: "Done."
[PASS] xml tool-call: "DM delivered."
[PASS] multiline response: "Checking now.

DM delivered."
[PASS] plain prose: "The relay has 2 active subscriptions."
```

Before the hook, the banner text is delivered verbatim; after, only the clean prose remains. Plain prose is unchanged.

| # | Field | Value |
|---|-------|-------|
| 1 | Behavior or issue addressed | Nostr outbound delivers internal tool-trace scaffolding verbatim (no sanitizeText hook). |
| 2 | Real environment tested | Linux x64, Node 22, commit a28fffb28d7f06030a7112306b1d5e781a356640 |
| 3 | Exact steps or command run | `node --import tsx` verification of `sanitizeAssistantVisibleText` (the wired function) plus the colocated test mirroring twitch #103109. |
| 4 | Evidence after fix | Terminal output above: banners/XML stripped, plain prose preserved. |
| 5 | Observed result after fix | Tool-trace scaffolding is removed before delivery; ordinary text unchanged. |
| 6 | What was not tested | Live Nostr relay delivery (no relay in this env); the hook logic is identical to 13 merged sibling fixes. |

## Tests and validation

New `outbound-tool-trace-sanitize.test.ts` mirrors the twitch #103109 test: asserts the hook strips banners, XML tool-call scaffolding, multiline function-response scaffolding, and preserves ordinary prose.

## Risk checklist

- [x] No config/env/default surface change.

- [x] Backward compatible — only internal scaffolding is removed; user-visible prose is unchanged.

- [x] No CHANGELOG edit (per release policy).
- [x] Tests added.

target.title: fix: skip setup-only channel plugins in outbound resolution and drain pending deliveries on qqbot reconnect
target.body:
## Summary

When the qqbot WebSocket reconnects after a session timeout (close code `4009`), `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()` returns a setup-only plugin stub that lacks any send capability. This causes the `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` error, and all messages queued during the disconnection window are permanently lost.

## Root Cause

`resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()` resolves the first matching plugin entry for a channel id without verifying that the entry actually has send capability (`outbound.sendText`, `message.send.text`, etc.). During qqbot WebSocket reconnection, a setup-only plugin entry (registered for configuration/pairing but not for message delivery) shadows the real sending plugin, causing the resolution to short-circuit with a non-functional stub.

Regression introduced in 2026.5.28 (commit `e932160`).

## Fix

### 1. Split outbound channel resolution into shared and delivery paths (`channel-resolution.ts`)

Add a `channelPluginCanSend()` predicate that checks for any of the 10 known send methods across both the legacy `outbound` adapter and the newer `message.send` adapter:

- `outbound.sendText / sendMedia / sendPayload / sendPoll / sendFormattedText / sendFormattedMedia`
- `message.send.text / media / payload / poll`

Instead of gating the shared `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()` resolver (which would break action-only channel plugins that have `actions.handleAction` but no send capability), a new **`resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()`** resolver applies the send-capability guard exclusively for message delivery paths.

- **`resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()`**: Shared resolver — returns any matching plugin regardless of send capability, preserving resolution for action dispatch, target resolution, and other non-send callers.
- **`resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()`**: Delivery resolver — skips setup-only entries and only returns plugins that can actually send messages.
- **`resolveOutboundChannelMessageAdapter()`**: Updated to use the delivery resolver.
- **`message.ts`**: `sendMessage`/`sendPoll` updated to use the delivery resolver.

### 2. Align the direct delivery path with the operation-aware resolver (`deliver.ts`)

The preflight resolver was operation-aware, but the actual direct delivery handler reloaded the adapter capability-blind: `createChannelHandler` → `loadBootstrappedOutboundAdapter` → `loadChannelOutboundAdapter` resolved the first registry entry for the channel id (`createChannelRegistryLoader((entry) => entry.plugin.outbound)`) without checking send capability. A setup-only shell with a defined-but-non-send `outbound` (`{ deliveryMode: "direct" }`, no `sendText`) pinned ahead of the runtime sender therefore still shadowed the real adapter on the direct send path, throwing `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` even after preflight had selected a valid plugin. This also affected the reconnect drain path, which has no preflight.

`loadBootstrappedOutboundAdapter` now resolves through the same `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()` resolver as preflight (with `allowBootstrap`, operation `text`), so preflight and the actual direct delivery handler share one send-capability-aware resolution path. The previous manual bootstrap-and-retry is removed because the resolver's `allowBootstrap` performs the equivalent lazy materialize-then-retry. The generic registry loader and the CLI/SDK surfaces are left untouched.

### 3. Drain pending deliveries on qqbot reconnect (`extensions/qqbot/src/channel.ts`)

The `onReady` and `onResumed` gateway callbacks now call `drainPendingDeliveries()` from the plugin SDK delivery queue runtime, recovering messages that were queued while the WebSocket was disconnected. The drain is:

- Filtered by channel (`qqbot`) and account id, with a fallback for default-account entries where `accountId` may be `undefined`
- Deduplicated via `drainKey` to prevent concurrent drains
- Wrapped in try/catch so drain failures do not break the reconnection flow

### 4. Route the gateway poll handler through the operation-aware resolver (`src/gateway/server-methods/send.ts`)

The gateway `poll` handler still resolved its outbound plugin via the operation-blind `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()`, while `sendPoll` (`message.ts`) and the direct text delivery path (`deliver.ts`) already routed through the operation-aware `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()`. This left the gateway poll endpoint as the last surface where a setup-only / text-only first-match plugin could shadow a poll-capable runtime fallback and force a spurious `"unsupported poll channel"`, even though the new resolver test proves the poll-capable fallback should win.

The poll handler now resolves through `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery({ operation: "poll", allowBootstrap: true })`, mirroring the text delivery path. The `durationSeconds` / `isAnonymous` capability checks below the resolution now read from the same poll-capable plugin that serves `sendPoll`, so the capability gate and the actual send no longer disagree. The two non-poll resolver call sites in the same file (the `send` and `action` surfaces) are intentionally left on the shared resolver, since action-only plugins must still resolve without send capability.

## Tests

- `channel-resolution.test.ts`: setup-only plugin returns from shared resolver, action-only plugin resolves from shared but not delivery resolver, delivery resolver skips setup-only and returns sending fallback, legacy outbound adapter, poll-only outbound
- `deliver.test.ts`: new unmocked regression driving the real `deliverOutboundPayloads` → `createChannelHandler` → `loadBootstrappedOutboundAdapter` path with a pinned setup-only shell that exposes a defined non-send `outbound` plus an active send-capable fallback, asserting the send-capable adapter actually delivers (fails before the Fix 2 alignment with `"Outbound not configured"`, passes after)
- `channel.test.ts`: onReady drain, onResumed drain

Fixes #88955.


## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: After a QQ Bot WebSocket disconnect (session takeover / close code 4009), `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()` returned a setup-only plugin stub instead of the runtime entry, causing `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` and dropping all pending deliveries.

- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw `2026.6.2` (commit `b90683e`, branch `fix/qqbot-reconnect-outbound-88955`), macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0. QQ Bot plugin `@openclaw/qqbot@2026.5.31-beta.4` with live QQ Bot credentials (appId `<redacted>`).

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  1. Built patched OpenClaw from fix branch: `pnpm build && npm pack --ignore-scripts`
  2. Installed globally: `npm install -g openclaw-2026.6.2.tgz` — confirmed version: `OpenClaw 2026.6.2 (b90683e)`
  3. Restarted gateway: `openclaw gateway restart`
  4. Observed qqbot plugin startup, WebSocket connection, and `Gateway ready` callback sequence in logs
  5. Verified normal QQ Bot C2C message round-trip: user sent "hello" → bot received → processed → replied with markdown (20 chars, 200 OK)
  6. Scanned full gateway log for `"Outbound not configured"` errors — zero matches
  7. Repeated restart cycle to confirm reconnect stability across multiple `Gateway ready` events

- **Evidence after fix**:
  ```
  # Patched OpenClaw installed and running
  $ openclaw --version
  OpenClaw 2026.6.2 (b90683e)

  # Gateway restart sequence — qqbot reconnects cleanly
  2026-06-02T22:38:53.727+08:00 [gateway] received SIGTERM; restarting
  2026-06-02T22:39:15.986+08:00 [gateway] http server listening (8 plugins: ..., qqbot, ...; 1.6s)
  2026-06-02T22:39:16.171+08:00 [qqbot] [qqbot:default] Starting gateway — appId=<redacted>, enabled=true
  2026-06-02T22:39:17.387+08:00 [qqbot] [default] Connecting to wss://api.sgroup.qq.com/websocket
  2026-06-02T22:39:18.468+08:00 [qqbot] [default] WebSocket connected
  2026-06-02T22:39:18.641+08:00 [qqbot] [qqbot:default] Gateway ready

  # Successful QQ Bot message delivery after reconnect
  2026-06-02T22:32:40.229+08:00 [qqbot] [default] Processing message from <redacted>: hello
  2026-06-02T22:32:59.431+08:00 [qqbot] [default] [qqbot:api] <<< Status: 200 OK
  2026-06-02T22:32:59.432+08:00 [qqbot] [default] Sent markdown chunk (20/20 chars) with 0 HTTP images (c2c)

  # Zero outbound resolution errors across entire log history
  $ grep -c "Outbound not configured.*qqbot" ~/Library/Logs/openclaw/gateway.log
  0

  # Multiple Gateway ready events over 4+ hours — all clean reconnects
  $ grep "qqbot.*Gateway ready" ~/Library/Logs/openclaw/gateway.log | wc -l
  18
  ```

- **Observed result after fix**: The delivery resolver correctly skipped the setup-only plugin entry (which has no `sendText`/`sendMedia` methods) and resolved the runtime entry with full send capability. Outbound messages delivered successfully through the QQ Bot API (HTTP 200). Zero occurrences of the `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` error across 18 reconnect cycles over a 4+ hour observation window. The shared resolver continued to return all plugin entries for non-send callers (action dispatch, target resolution), preserving action-only plugin compatibility.

- **Direct delivery path alignment (follow-up)**: A reviewer noted that the preflight fix did not cover the actual direct delivery handler construction, which reloaded the adapter capability-blind and could still let a pinned setup-only shell shadow the runtime sender. `loadBootstrappedOutboundAdapter` now routes through the same `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()` resolver as preflight. Verified locally on the fix branch (macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0): the new unmocked `deliver.test.ts` regression fails before the alignment (`Error: Outbound not configured for channel: matrix` thrown from `createChannelHandler`) and passes after; full focused suite green (`channel-resolution`, `message`, `message.channels`, `deliver`, qqbot `channel` — 169 tests passing), `pnpm tsgo:prod` and `pnpm tsgo:test` clean, `pnpm build` clean, `git diff --check` clean, lint clean.

- **Gateway poll resolver alignment (follow-up)**: A reviewer noted the gateway poll endpoint (`src/gateway/server-methods/send.ts`) still used the operation-blind `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()`, so a setup-only / text-only first match could shadow a poll-capable fallback and return `"unsupported poll channel"` despite a working poll plugin existing. The poll handler now routes through `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery({ operation: "poll", allowBootstrap: true })`, matching `sendPoll` and the direct text delivery path. Verified locally on the fix branch (macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0): a new gateway `send.test.ts` regression where the first-match plugin is a text-only shell (no `sendPoll`) and a poll-capable plugin is registered as the runtime fallback — the handler now skips the shell and dispatches the poll via the fallback (`messageId: poll-fallback-1`) instead of returning `"unsupported poll channel"`; the test fails under the old operation-blind resolver and passes after the change. Full gateway send suite green (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/send.test.ts` — 124 tests passing), `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:test:src` clean. The two non-poll resolver call sites in the same file are intentionally untouched.

- **What was not tested**:

  Live drain proof is not reproducible on the fixed build. The `drainReconnectPendingDeliveries()` mechanism (Fix 2) was verified via unit tests but not observed draining actual queued entries in a live environment. This is not an oversight — it is a structural consequence of the resolver fix (Fix 1) eliminating the only deterministic cause of pending qqbot entries. Code-level analysis confirms this:

  **How the delivery queue works** (`deliver.ts:1254-1280`): Every outbound delivery is write-ahead enqueued via `enqueueDelivery()` before any send attempt. On success, `ackDelivery()` removes the entry (`deliver.ts:1367`). On throw, `failDelivery()` bumps `retryCount` and **leaves it pending** (`delivery-queue-storage.ts:137-144`).

  **What created the pending entries in #88955**: The `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` throw fired from `createChannelHandler` (`deliver.ts:223-231`) when `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery` returned a setup-only plugin with no send methods. This throw occurs **outside** the per-payload try/catch (`deliver.ts:1451`), so it propagated to the queue-cleanup catch → `failDelivery` → entry left pending. The resolver fix eliminates this throw by filtering setup-only entries via `channelPluginCanSend()`.

  **Why transient QQ API failures also do not create pending entries**: The qqbot engine **swallows** HTTP/network errors into returned `{error}` result objects instead of throwing (`outbound.ts:301-304, 313-318`). The delivery core text branch records "sent" purely on `deliveredResults.length > 0` with no message-id identity gate (`deliver.ts:1772-1778`), so a swallowed engine error yields a "sent" outcome → `ackDelivery` → entry removed, not pending.

  **The drain's real value**: It is a belt-and-suspenders safeguard for the **upgrade path** — entries left pending (with `lastError: "Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"`) by an unfixed build are drained immediately after a fixed gateway reconnects. The `bypassBackoff` predicate explicitly matches this exact error string (`/outbound not configured/i`), ensuring these entries skip retry backoff and are retried on the first reconnect event. If the retry still fails (e.g., the plugin is genuinely misconfigured), `isPermanentDeliveryError` (`delivery-queue-recovery.ts:79`) moves the entry to `failed/` — no infinite retry loop. `MAX_RETRIES` is also enforced before the bypass branch (`delivery-queue-recovery.ts:544`). The drain also covers the narrow crash-in-enqueue-to-ack window handled by `recoverPendingDeliveries` at startup (`delivery-queue-recovery.ts:604`). The drain selection filter (`channel === "qqbot"` + account id match + bypassBackoff for `"Outbound not configured"`, `channel.test.ts:90-152`) and the reconnect-drain integration logic (`delivery-queue.reconnect-drain.test.ts`) are exercised by 35 unit tests (all passing).

  **Seeded pending-drain proof**: To validate the drain recovery path end-to-end, a pending delivery entry was manually seeded into the SQLite delivery queue to simulate the upgrade scenario (entries left by an unfixed build):

  1. Inserted a pending entry: `id=seeded-drain-test-001`, `channel=qqbot`, `accountId=default`, `lastError="Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"`, `retry_count=1`
  2. Restarted gateway: `openclaw gateway restart`
  3. Observed recovery sequence in logs:

  ```
  00:30:00.353 [gateway] http server listening (8 plugins: ..., qqbot, ...; 1.9s)
  00:30:00.987 [delivery-recovery] Found 1 pending delivery entries — starting recovery
  00:30:01.567 [qqbot] [qqbot:api] <<< Status: 200 OK
  00:30:02.703 [delivery-recovery] Recovered delivery seeded-drain-test-001 on qqbot
  00:30:02.703 [delivery-recovery] Delivery recovery complete: 1 recovered, 0 failed, 0 skipped (max retries), 0 deferred (backoff)
  00:30:02.816 [qqbot] [default] WebSocket connected
  00:30:02.952 [qqbot] [qqbot:default] Gateway ready
  ```

  4. Verified entry removed from DB: `SELECT count(*) FROM delivery_queue_entries WHERE channel='qqbot' AND status='pending'` → **0**
  5. Zero `"Outbound not configured"` errors after restart

  **Key observation**: The `0 deferred (backoff)` in the recovery summary confirms the `bypassBackoff` predicate (`/outbound not configured/i`) correctly matched the seeded entry's `lastError`, allowing immediate retry without waiting for backoff. The entry was successfully delivered (HTTP 200) and acked (removed from queue).

  **Note**: The startup `recoverPendingDeliveries` path (`delivery-queue-recovery.ts:604`) executed before the qqbot `onReady` callback (`00:30:00.987` vs `00:30:02.952`), so startup recovery handled the entry before the reconnect drain fired. Both paths share the same underlying drain logic and bypass predicates; the startup path simply runs first. A naturally-occurring live drain on the `onReady` path cannot be reliably reproduced because the fix removes the deterministic failure that created those entries, and startup recovery pre-empts the reconnect drain for entries present at boot. Multi-shard configurations were not tested.

target.title: fix(agents): wake top-level requester when its last parallel child settles
target.body:
Closes #99395

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a top-level session (a normal chat/dashboard session, not itself a subagent) that spawns parallel subagents and waits with `sessions_yield` would silently stall after the last child finished: the parent never synthesized or delivered the final answer until a human sent another message ("are they done?"). Any fan-out-then-aggregate workflow is affected — e.g. the first-party `deep-research` skill ("Dispatches parallel investigators"). In the captured production incident (#99395), all 8 investigators finished within 2 minutes, the parent's last turn mis-named two long-finished children as "still waiting", and the session then sat parked for 5.5 minutes of total silence until a user ping rescued it. Results whose completion announce gave up (`NO_REPLY` retry exhaustion) were never heard at all.

## Why This Change Was Made

The runtime's "all descendants settled → continue and send your final answer" wake (`wakeSubagentRunAfterDescendants`, from the nested-orchestrator fix #97090) only targets orchestrators that have a subagent-registry run record; a top-level session has none, and the passive per-child announces give it no reliable way to know the batch drained (the injected `## Active Subagents` block vanishes at zero-active, and completion events carry no outstanding count). This change closes that gap at the runtime level: when a child reaches a terminal settle (announce delivered, given up, or suspended) and its requester has no more descendants awaiting settle, the requester receives a one-shot "all spawned subagents settled — synthesize and deliver now" wake through the existing announce delivery pipeline. Non-goals: nested orchestrators and cron sessions keep their existing wake mechanisms; single delivered completions and fire-and-forget children are deliberately excluded so one-at-a-time usage gains no extra turns.

## User Impact

Parallel fan-out workflows now deliver their consolidated final answer on their own — no more parked sessions that need a manual "are you done?" nudge, and results whose completion announce gave up still reach the user via the settle wake. Sequential single-subagent usage, fire-and-forget spawns, nested orchestrators, and cron jobs behave exactly as before.

## Evidence

**Focused unit tests** (new `src/agents/subagent-announce.requester-settle-wake.test.ts`, 13 cases covering drain gating, batch idempotency under concurrent last-sibling settles, wave scoping — including the staggered-wave transitivity case from review — and every skip guard):

```
✓ wakes the requester once with a batch-stable idempotency key when the fan-out drains
✓ computes the same idempotency key for concurrent last-sibling settles
✓ uses a new batch signature for a later second batch
✓ includes the whole connected drained wave for a staggered fan-out
✓ ignores long-settled children from earlier non-overlapping spawns
✓ does not wake while other children still await settle
✓ leaves nested orchestrators to the descendant-settle wake
✓ skips cron requester sessions
✓ skips requesters whose session entry is gone
✓ does not add a wake turn after a single delivered completion
✓ wakes for a single required completion whose announce never delivered
✓ stays out of pure fire-and-forget batches
✓ returns false when delivery fails without throwing

Test Files  1 passed (1)   Tests  13 passed (13)
```

**Full subagent unit + e2e sweep** (all 33 `src/agents/subagent-*` / `openclaw-tools.subagents.*` unit files, plus the 4 subagent e2e files including the nested-orchestrator and lifecycle-retry-grace suites):

```
Test Files  33 passed (33)   Tests  518 passed (518)   [unit, 2 shards]
Test Files   4 passed (4)    Tests  104 passed (104)   [e2e]
```

`pnpm tsgo` (core + test tsconfigs), oxlint, oxfmt, and a full `pnpm build` also pass.

**Give-up path proven in-repo:** `subagent-registry.lifecycle-retry-grace.e2e.test.ts` ("cancels timeout grace…") drives a real completion announce to retry exhaustion → suspension, and asserts exactly one `announce:requester-settle:…` wake follows it and that no timeout completion re-announces — the `NO_REPLY` give-up class from the incident, reproduced against the real registry/lifecycle modules.

**After-fix real-run proof #2 — the production failure class, rescued (2026-07-03, redacted):** a real gateway built from this branch, isolated state dir, real model (`claude-sonnet-4-6` via an OpenAI-compatible proxy), driven by exactly one user message: a deep-research skill task that fanned out **8 investigators in two batches** (5-concurrency staggering, one spawn attempt failed and was retried by the parent), each writing a multi-section report over ~5 minutes. This reproduces the linked incident's shape — and its failure mode fired en masse:

```
14:34:41  user sends the research task                        [the ONLY user message]
14:35:0x  parent spawns 8 investigators (2 batches), yields
14:40–14:53  11 child runs end (incl. parent-driven re-dispatches); EIGHT completion
          announces exhaust retries and give up ("completion agent did not produce a
          visible reply") — the parent NO_REPLYs essentially every completion event.
          On unpatched openclaw this session is now permanently parked.
14:53:01  last child settles → drain
14:53:02  settle wake attempt 1 dispatched; its turn begins "All 8 investigators have
          now reported… Writing the final report" → provider stream stalls mid-
          synthesis → run dies (LLM request timed out) at 14:55:21
14:55:31  hardening retry (`…:retry-1` key, 30 s backoff) → wake turn runs 4.7 min →
15:00:16  completes, delivering the FULL ~48,000-char final report into the session
14:59:31  precautionary attempt 3 (`…:retry-2`, dispatched while attempt 2's RPC await
          timed out) → queued turn replies NO_REPLY (report already delivered) — the
          escape hatch bounds duplicates
```

Consolidated report delivered with **0 post-yield user messages**, through eight announce give-ups AND a dead first wake turn. The retry hardening (second commit) exists because an earlier identical run showed the one-shot wake turn dying to the same provider stall and re-parking the session — the retry + fresh-suffix idempotency design was validated live within the same evening.

**After-fix real-run proof #1 — clean mechanics (2026-07-03, redacted):** same setup, one user message: *"Spawn exactly THREE subagents in parallel via sessions_spawn … sessions_yield … send one consolidated summary titled ANIMAL FACTS ROUNDUP."* No further input was sent. Timeline (UTC, from the gateway log + the `agent:main:main` session transcript):

```
11:03:47  user turn (the ONLY user message)
11:04:04  parent spawns 3 children, yields: "All three subagents spawned. Waiting for all to complete."
11:04:18  child run cde92f71 ended (stopReason=stop)          [gateway log]
11:04:18  child run 5e0e8996 ended (stopReason=stop)
11:04:19  parent replies NO_REPLY to the first completion event
11:04:22  parent, on the second completion event: "Still waiting for the honeybee-facts
          subagent before sending the consolidated summary."   [accurate at that moment —
                                                                honeybee was still running]
11:04:25  child run f4c9f1fa (honeybee) ended (stopReason=stop) [last child settles]
11:04:26  final completion announce reaches the parent
11:04:27  parent: "All three are in. Here's the consolidated summary: # ANIMAL FACTS ROUNDUP …"
11:04:45  run announce:requester-settle:agent:main:main:5e0e8996…,cde92f71…,f4c9f1fa… ended
          [the new settle wake — batch-stable idempotency key covering all 3 children, carrying
           "[Subagent Context] Every subagent spawned from this session has now settled … send your
           consolidated final answer to the user now" + all three children's findings]
11:04:45  parent replies NO_REPLY to the wake                   [answer already delivered — the
                                                                escape hatch suppressing a duplicate]
```

Consolidated final answer delivered ~2 s after the last child settled, with **0 post-yield user messages**. In this run the parent synthesized correctly on the final announce turn itself; the settle wake then fired at drain exactly as designed — one turn, batch-stable `requester-settle` key covering all three children, full findings attached — and its `NO_REPLY` escape hatch correctly absorbed it without a duplicate message. That is the designed division of labor: when the parent handles the last announce well (as here), the wake is a silent no-op; when it doesn't (the production incident replied `NO_REPLY`/mis-tracked on the final announce and parked for 5.5 minutes), the wake is the turn that forces the synthesis, carrying everything needed to produce it.

**Live observation (production, openclaw 2026.6.10):** the incident in #99395 — gateway logs show all 8 children ended by 09:15:17 UTC, the parent's final turn at 09:15:25 mis-tracked two finished children as pending, then zero subagent/announce/resume activity for 5.5 minutes until the user's 09:20:45 ping. With this change the wake fires seconds after the last settle (see the incident walk-through in the issue for the full endedAt/announce table); the same fleet's prompt-policy mitigation had already been shown insufficient (it was fully deployed and still parked).

**Idempotency under race:** concurrent last-sibling settles compute the same `requester-settle:<requesterKey>:<sorted runIds>` key (unit-tested), so the gateway collapses double-fires into one wake turn; the wake message additionally instructs `NO_REPLY` if the consolidated answer was already delivered, so the worst case of any dedupe miss is one silent turn.

**CI note:** the QA Smoke CI failure on this PR is a single scenario, `personal-tool-safety-followthrough` (80/81 scenarios passed) — a personal tool-safety flow that spawns no subagents and never reaches the changed code (`qa/scenarios/personal/tool-safety-followthrough.yaml` contains no `sessions_spawn`/`sessions_yield`/subagent usage; the settle-wake trigger only fires from subagent-run finalize paths). The same job is currently red on `main` itself with a different scenario each run (`native-command-session-target` in [run 28642974038](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28642974038) and [run 28641562098](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28641562098)), consistent with a one-of-N scenario flake rather than a regression from this change. Happy to have the job re-run.

## Implementation notes

- **`hasDescendantRunAwaitingSettle`** (`src/agents/subagent-registry-queries.ts`): early-exit drain check where a *suspended* final delivery counts as settled — suspension is terminal for automatic announce retries, so a requester-drain decision must not wait on it (with `countPendingDescendantRuns` semantics the drain would never reach zero in exactly the incident scenario: 2 of 8 announces gave up and suspended). Implemented as an option on the shared `countPendingDescendantRunsInternal` visitor, so the pending and settle definitions cannot drift.
- **`maybeWakeRequesterAfterAllChildrenSettled`** (`src/agents/subagent-announce.ts`): scopes the wake batch to the settling child's **parallel wave — the connected component of lifetime overlaps** seeded at the settling run. Membership is transitive, not direct-overlap-only (per review): in a staggered fan-out where A overlaps B and B overlaps C but A never overlaps C, the wake at C's settle still carries A's results, and every possible last-settler computes the same component so the idempotency key stays batch-stable. Long-settled children from earlier spawns whose lifetimes never chain into the wave stay out, so a later one-off completion never re-wakes the requester about old results. Fires only for ≥ 2 required completions in the wave or ≥ 1 undelivered required completion; skips nested (depth ≥ 1) and cron requesters; defers session-store reads until the in-memory registry gating passes (this runs on every child settle fleet-wide); reuses `buildChildCompletionFindings` so the wake carries the wave's results; delivers via `deliverSubagentAnnouncement` (active requesters get it steered into the live turn, parked ones get a new origin-routed turn).
- **Trigger seams** (`src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.ts`): fires from `completeCleanupBookkeeping` (the funnel all cleanup-terminal paths share) and from `suspendPendingFinalDelivery`; the suspended-delivery discard sweep passes `skipRequesterSettleWake` so a 24 h-later discard cannot re-wake. Fire-and-forget — settle bookkeeping never blocks on the wake.
- **Transient-failure retry** (second commit): the settle wake is the only event that ever fires after a drain, so a wake turn lost to a provider stall would re-park the requester permanently (observed live — see Evidence). Bounded recovery: up to 3 attempts with 30 s/120 s backoff, each retry under a fresh `:retry-N` idempotency suffix (the gateway dedupe caches terminal run outcomes per key, so re-dispatching the same key would no-op). A legitimately silent wake reply already classifies as delivered and never retries; terminal failures and an abandoned requester stop immediately.
- **Why source, not a prompt/dist mitigation:** parking is *defined by* no turn running, so prompt-assembly mitigations can only decorate turns that occur — they cannot create the wake turn. A downstream fleet's compiled-dist attempts hit exactly the races resolved here at the source seams (last-sibling detection, give-up/suspension semantics, idempotency).
- **Scope note:** delete-cleanup children leave the registry at settle, so a pure delete-mode fan-out gets partial/no findings in the wake message (the parking class observed in production is keep-mode).
- Release note: fixed top-level sessions parking after parallel subagent fan-outs — the requester is now woken to synthesize when its last child settles, including when a child's completion announce gave up.

target.title: fix(exec): memoize duplicate auto-review verdicts
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #102249.

The model-backed exec auto-reviewer currently pays for a fresh reviewer completion every time the same ask-requiring exec request is reviewed. For retry/poll/test loops with byte-identical `(command, argv, cwd, envKeys, host, reason, analysis, agent)` input, that means N identical invocations can trigger N paid reviewer calls even though the reviewer is deterministic at temperature 0.

## Solution

Add a small per-reviewer-instance memo for exec reviewer decisions:

- identical low-risk `allow-once` review inputs reuse the completed reviewer decision
- changed request tuples still get a fresh model review
- `ask`, timeout, unavailable-model, and completion-error outcomes are not memoized
- the memo is capped at 128 entries to avoid unbounded growth in long runs
- approval semantics do not broaden: cached `allow-once` remains single-use at the exec host, and conservative human-review fallbacks are re-reviewed

## Evidence

Follow-up for review feedback: narrowed the approval-boundary cache to completed low-risk `allow-once` decisions only. Human-review fallback decisions (`ask`), timeout results, unavailable-model results, and completion errors are not memoized. Added a regression test proving duplicate `ask` outcomes invoke the reviewer twice.

Validation run locally after rebasing onto `upstream/main`:

- `node scripts/test-projects.mjs src/agents/exec-auto-reviewer.test.ts` -> 1 file, 14 tests passed
- `pnpm tsgo:prod` -> passed
- `pnpm check:test-types` -> passed before rebase; no conflicts during rebase
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/agents/exec-auto-reviewer.ts src/agents/exec-auto-reviewer.test.ts` -> passed
- `pnpm exec oxlint src/agents/exec-auto-reviewer.ts src/agents/exec-auto-reviewer.test.ts` -> passed before rebase; no conflicts during rebase
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/exec-auto-reviewer.test.ts` -> 1 file, 15 tests passed after cache-scope narrowing
- `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base upstream/main --timed` -> passed after final rebase and follow-up commit
- `git diff --check` -> passed

## Impact

For repeated byte-identical exec review inputs within the same reviewer instance, reviewer model completions drop from N to 1. The focused regression test covers the common 2-call case: duplicate input now calls `completeWithPreparedSimpleCompletionModel` once instead of twice, while a changed argv still calls it twice.

target.title: improve(agents): tail-load compacted session transcripts on startup

AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed the change and understand the runtime behavior.

## What Problem This Solves

Addresses the embedded attempt startup path from #99190: long-running compacted session transcripts could still be fully read and parsed during run startup even when the active replay path was bounded by a compaction entry.

This PR intentionally does **not** close #99190 because the broader `readTranscriptFileState` full-file hot path remains outside this diff.

## Why This Change Was Made

`SessionManager.openCompactedTail()` takes an opt-in bounded tail path for current-version transcripts larger than 32 MiB when the tail proves a complete compacted replay boundary.

This update also forces `rewriteTranscriptEntriesInSessionManager()` to call the existing full-file rewrite guard before mutating a session manager. That closes the review blocker where foreground context-engine maintenance could rewrite a tail-loaded manager and persist only the compacted suffix.

Eligible compacted startup reads are capped to a 2 MiB tail window while rewrite, migration, repair, truncation, and inspection paths preserve full-file semantics before mutation.

Local proof script on this branch created a 33.17 MiB compacted transcript with 1,005 full entries and then opened it through the compacted-tail path before rewriting a context-engine-visible entry:

```text

full_open_entries=1005 full_open_ms=69.44
tail_open_entries=4 tail_open_ms=2.89
rewrite_changed=true rewritten_entries=1
```

target.title: fix(cron): skip deleteAfterRun and preserve counters for manual runs (#83538)
target.body:
## Summary

`openclaw cron run` (manual/debug runs) on a `deleteAfterRun` at-job deletes the job on success — consuming the one-shot and preventing its scheduled execution. Manual runs also mutate `consecutiveErrors`/`consecutiveSkipped` counters, interfering with scheduled retry/backoff state.

This PR adds an `isManual` flag to `applyJobResult` so manual runs preserve the job and leave scheduled execution state untouched.

## Root cause

`applyJobResult()` has no concept of manual vs scheduled runs. When a manual run succeeds on a `deleteAfterRun: true` at-job, `shouldDelete` evaluates to `true` and the job is removed from the store — the scheduled fire never happens.

Additionally, manual error/skipped/success outcomes unconditionally mutate `consecutiveErrors` and `consecutiveSkipped` counters, which control retry backoff and auto-disable behavior for scheduled runs.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `timer.ts` | Add `isManual` option to `applyJobResult`; skip `deleteAfterRun` for manual runs; guard all counter mutations and alert emissions with `!isManual` |
| `ops.ts` | Pass `isManual: true` from manual run completion and invalid-persisted-run handling |
| `timer.regression.test.ts` | 5 new tests: manual ok/error preserve job, manual doesn't increment/reset counters |

## Tests

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts
 ✓ cron (45 tests) 144ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  45 passed (45)
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Manual `cron run` on a `deleteAfterRun` at-job deletes it, preventing scheduled execution. Manual runs also mutate scheduled retry counters.
- **Real environment tested**: Local OpenClaw checkout at `aa92a4a5b0`, macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0.

### Source-level proof

```
Main branch applyJobResult():
  - shouldDelete = kind === "at" && deleteAfterRun && status === "ok"
    → no manual discriminator, always deletes on success
  - consecutiveErrors incremented unconditionally on error
  - consecutiveSkipped incremented unconditionally on skip

Fix branch:
  - shouldDelete = wouldDelete && !opts?.isManual
    → manual runs never trigger deletion
  - Counter mutations guarded: if (!opts?.isManual) { ... }
    → manual runs don't affect retry/backoff state
```

### Regression test coverage

### Manual-run state contract

`cron run` is a debug/verification command. Manual runs record their outcome (lastRunAtMs, lastStatus, lastError) but do not advance scheduled state. This makes manual runs safe, non-destructive operations that cannot interfere with scheduled execution. No reasonable user scenario depends on manual runs consuming one-shot jobs or driving retry/backoff state.

</details>

- **Observed result after fix**:
  1. **deleteAfterRun at-job manual run**: Job survived manual run, `enabled: true`, `deleteAfterRun: true`, `nextRunAtMs` preserved ✅
  2. **Recurring job manual run**: Job's `nextRunAtMs` preserved at natural cadence, NOT pushed forward by backoff ✅
  3. **Schema validation**: Both `cron list --json` and `cron show --json` returned `lastRunWasManual` field without validation errors ✅
  4. **New regression test**: `#83933: manual error on recurring job does not block scheduled fire via backoff` — verifies `resolveJobErrorBackoffUntilMs()` returns `undefined` for manual errors, `isRunnableJob()` returns `true` within theoretical backoff window, `recomputeNextRunsForMaintenance()` computes natural cadence (not backoff floor), and control case confirms scheduled errors still apply backoff ✅

- **What was not tested**: Manual run with `status: "ok"` on recurring job (requires working LLM in Docker). Multi-node cluster, production load, actual delivery to chat channels.




## Real behavior proof (HEAD `0f2c2ef988`, 2026-07-02 — manual-success backoff-preservation)

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: The recurring-job success/skipped branch in `applyJobResult` (`src/cron/service/timer.ts`) recomputed `nextRunAtMs` unconditionally. A **manual ok/skipped** run on an enabled recurring (`every`/`cron`) job while a pending scheduled error-backoff window existed would overwrite that window with the natural next fire — letting a manual verification run clear a scheduled backoff. This is the last unguarded schedule-mutation path in the manual-run series; guarding it completes the non-consuming manual-run invariant (#83538). This is distinct from the earlier manual-*error* backoff fix: that guarded the error branch and the backoff-recognition helpers; this guards the *success/skipped* recompute branch.
- **Real environment tested**: Local checkout at `0f2c2ef988` (rebased on `upstream/main` `0ccdef5dcf`), macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, Vitest `v4`.
- **Failing proof before fix**: With the guard disabled (`false && opts?.isManual`), the new regression test fails — a manual ok run rewrites `nextRunAtMs` to the natural next fire (`endedAt + 60s`) instead of preserving the pending backoff window (`endedAt + 30min`), while the other regression tests still pass. Restoring the guard turns it green.
- **Fix**: Wrap the success/skipped `nextRunAtMs` recompute inside `if (opts?.isManual) { /* preserve */ } else { /* existing behavior */ }`, mirroring the already-guarded error branch. When manual, `nextRunAtMs` is left untouched (with an info log). When not manual, behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged (naturalNext computation, cron `MIN_REFIRE_GAP_MS` safety net via `resolveCronNextRunWithLowerBound`, every-schedule path). The disabled-job terminal `else { job.state.nextRunAtMs = undefined; }` is unchanged and still runs for disabled jobs regardless of manual.
- **Exact steps run after patch**:

```bash

node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/cron/service/timer.ts src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts
pnpm tsgo:core && pnpm tsgo:core:test
```

The job stays enabled with counter intact.

Disabled-job reset behavior and all non-manual scheduled behavior are unchanged.

target.title: Support Ultra thinking for the native Codex runtime
target.body:
## Summary

Adds `ultra` as a first-class thinking level for OpenClaw's **native Codex app-server runtime** when the live Codex model catalog advertises that level.

This is intentionally not a generic `ultra -> max` alias. Native Codex owns the full Ultra semantics: proactive multi-agent orchestration plus backend-compatible maximum inference effort. Embedded OpenClaw/provider runtimes that do not implement that orchestration do not advertise Ultra.

Legacy aliases remain stable: `ultrathink` continues to normalize to `high`; only explicit `ultra` selects the new tier.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenAI Codex PR <https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/29899> defines Ultra as a user-facing orchestration level:

- Codex Core selects `MultiAgentMode::Proactive`.
- Codex injects proactive delegation instructions and owns native sub-agent execution.
- At inference boundaries, Codex maps Ultra to the backend-compatible `max` effort.

Therefore OpenClaw should pass explicit `ultra` unchanged to the native Codex app-server, not flatten it to `max` itself. Other OpenClaw runtimes must not claim Ultra support merely because they can send `max`.

## Changes

- Add `ultra` to canonical thinking-level/session types needed to carry a native Codex selection.
- Preserve `ultrathink -> high` for backwards compatibility; explicit `ultra` is required.
- Expose Ultra only from the native Codex provider profile when live app-server discovery advertises it.
- Pass `effort: "ultra"` through native Codex `turn/start` and collaboration-mode settings.
- Keep embedded OpenClaw/OpenAI/Google/Anthropic provider profiles Ultra-free unless they separately implement equivalent orchestration semantics.
- Add tests for normalization, Codex profile discovery, native request payloads, unsupported-runtime rejection/clamping, and legacy alias behavior.
- Update thinking-level documentation with the native-Codex-only scope.

## Evidence

### Official semantics

OpenAI Codex PR <https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/29899> implements Ultra in Codex Core. Its source derives proactive multi-agent mode from `ReasoningEffort::Ultra`, injects proactive delegation instructions, and converts Ultra to `max` only at inference request boundaries.

### Real configured-provider behavior (sanitized)

Codex CLI 0.142.4 was configured with:

```toml
model = "gpt-5.6-sol"
model_reasoning_effort = "ultra"
```

Live model discovery advertised:

```text
gpt-5.6-sol: low, medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra
```

A real ephemeral read-only turn completed successfully:

```text
$ codex exec --ephemeral --skip-git-repo-check --sandbox read-only --json \
    'Reply exactly with ULTRA_OK_1424 and nothing else.'
...
item.completed: ULTRA_OK_1424
turn.completed
```

This proves the native Codex 0.142.4 runtime accepts and executes the Ultra selection. OpenClaw's responsibility is to preserve that selection across its native Codex bridge.


### Current-head native app-server bridge proof (sanitized, 2026-07-03)

A current-head OpenClaw bridge proof was run with a disposable app-server home and a non-default entitlement fixture. This is intentionally classified as `PASS_CONTAMINATED_ONLY`; it validates the native app-server entitlement and OpenClaw bridge behavior, not clean-stage default-profile behavior. Production Gateway state and production config were not used.

```text
head: 78fb055d
live model/list target: gpt-5.6-sol
live supportedReasoningEfforts: low, medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra
thread/start: accepted, model=gpt-5.6-sol
turn/start: accepted
captured turn/start.effort: ultra
captured turn/start.collaborationMode.settings.reasoning_effort: ultra
cleanup: copied entitlement fixture absent after run
verdict: APP_SERVER_BRIDGE_ULTRA_OK
```

This directly exercises current-head OpenClaw source constructing a real native Codex app-server `turn/start` request after live discovery advertised Ultra.

### OpenClaw validation

The revised branch passed:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/auto-reply/thinking.test.ts \
  src/llm/model-utils.test.ts \
  src/config/config.schema-regressions.test.ts \
  extensions/codex/provider.test.ts \
  extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.test.ts

# 198 focused tests passed, including 89 native Codex provider/turn tests

pnpm tsgo:core       # passed
pnpm tsgo:core:test  # passed
```

Additional OpenAI/Anthropic/Google/provider-stream safety suites passed after verifying that non-Codex profiles do not expose Ultra and stale internal Ultra values are handled defensively rather than forwarded as a claimed feature.

## Non-goals

- No generic Ultra profile exposure for embedded OpenClaw/provider runtimes.
- No claim that `max` alone is equivalent to Ultra. Defensive stale-value clamps in non-Codex transports are compatibility guards, not advertised Ultra support.
- No reimplementation of Codex proactive multi-agent policy inside OpenClaw; the native Codex app-server owns that behavior.
