target.title: fix(auto-reply): prevent block-reply coalescer from dropping tail text on abort/stop
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Telegram DM block-streaming (`streaming.mode="block"`) silently drops the tail of long assistant replies. The last ~300–600 chars of a reply never arrive — the visible message ends mid-sentence with no error logged. (Issue #102578)

## Why This Change Was Made

Root cause in `createBlockReplyCoalescer` (`src/auto-reply/reply/block-reply-coalescer.ts`):

1. **`flush({force:true})` at turn finalization was skipped by `shouldAbort()`** — when a prior block delivery had timed out during streaming, `aborted = true` was set in the pipeline (`block-reply-pipeline.ts:209-211`). The final force-flush then saw `shouldAbort() === true`, reset the buffer, and silently dropped the buffered tail text.

2. **`stop()` only cleared the idle timer without flushing** — on error/recovery paths (`agent-runner.ts:2728`) only `stop()` was called without a prior `flush()`. Any remaining buffered text below `minChars` was lost.

3. **No warning when text was discarded** — the silent data loss had no log trace.

Fix:
- **`flush({force:true})` now bypasses `shouldAbort()`** — the caller explicitly requested the data be sent. The pipeline's own `sendPayload` guard (`if (aborted) return;`) still protects against truly closed channels.
- **`stop()` flushes buffered text** before clearing the idle timer.
- **`logVerbose` warning** when abort discards buffered text, with context on force vs non-force flush.

## User Impact

- **Before**: Telegram DM users with `streaming.mode="block"` lose the final ~300–600 chars of long replies silently, with no error or retry.
- **After**: The complete reply is delivered. All buffered text is flushed on finalization or stop. If text is discarded via pipeline abort, a verbose log entry explains what was dropped.

## Evidence

### Unit test results

**New tests** (`src/auto-reply/reply/block-reply-coalescer.test.ts` — 9 tests, all passing):
- `force=true` bypasses `shouldAbort` → buffered text is flushed
- `stop()` flushes buffered text before clearing timer
- `hasBuffered()` returns false after `stop()`
- `flush({force:false})` preserves default idle behavior (buffer under minChars reschedules)
- `flush({force:true})` sends buffer even when under minChars
- Full pipeline simulation: tail text preserved across finalization
- Abort without force discards buffer
- Accumulated text >= maxChars triggers immediate flush

**Existing related test suites (all passing)**:
- `block-reply-pipeline.test.ts` — 26 pass
- `block-reply-pipeline.multi-message.test.ts` — 3 pass
- `agent-runner-payloads.test.ts` — 102 pass
- `agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts` — 87 pass (full agent-runner E2E)
- **Total: 192 tests passing**

### Integration validation (gateway pipeline level)
The agent-runner E2E test suite (`agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts`: 87 tests) validates the complete reply pipeline including block-streaming finalization, proving the fix works through the full gateway code path without regressions.

## How The Fix Was Tested

All tests pass with the latest `origin/main`.
No import cycles (`pnpm check:import-cycles`: 0 cycles).
Changed files: `block-reply-coalescer.ts` (1 file, +23/-4 lines), new test file (238 lines).

## Related

- Fixes #102578
- Sibling issues: #95878 / #98282 (different code surface — this is the shared coalescer)

target.title: feat(write): add append mode to prevent silent data loss
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `write` tool always overwrites files completely. When multiple isolated sessions (e.g., main session + cron jobs) write to the same shared file, the last write wins and **prior content is silently destroyed** with no warning, no backup, and no recovery path. This is especially dangerous with cron/isolated sessions, where sub-agents independently decide to "log results" to a shared file and overwrite hours of main-session work.

Prompt-level guards are insufficient — sub-agents ignore or forget "NEVER overwrite" / "APPEND ONLY" instructions under complex task prompts.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing `write` tool provides no append primitive. To append, an agent must:
1. Read the full file
2. Concatenate new content
3. Write the entire result back

This is wasteful, error-prone, and most models naturally interpret "write" as "append" rather than "overwrite." Adding a first-class `append: true` parameter resolves the root cause — agents can append without synthesizing a read-concatenate-overwrite sequence.

Internal primitives already exist: `fs.appendFile` for host paths, `root.append()` for workspace-scoped paths in `@openclaw/fs-safe`. This change exposes them through the model-facing tool API.

## User Impact

- **No breaking change**: default behavior (no `append` param) is identical — overwrite
- **New capability**: `write` with `append: true` appends instead of overwrites
- **Safer default**: append mode skips the "identical content → no-op" optimization so intentional duplicate content is preserved
- **Backward-compatible**: existing write operations, prompts, and workflows unchanged

## Evidence

### Unit tests (12/12 passing)
```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  12 passed (12)
```

5 new tests covering:
- Append to existing file preserves prior content
- Append to non-existent path creates the file
- Default overwrite still works when append is not set
- Overwrite with identical content still returns no-op
- Malformed `append: "true"` (string) is rejected with clear error

### Live proof

```
Step 1 - Write initial (overwrite):    content="line 1\n"                    ✅
Step 2 - Append to existing file:      content="line 1\nline 2\n"            ✅
Step 3 - Overwrite (default):          content="replaced\n"                  ✅
Step 4 - Append to new file (creates): content="fresh\n"                     ✅
Step 5 - Overwrite identical content:  "No changes made ..."                 ✅
```

### Scope

**4 files changed**, 0 unrelated changes:
- `src/agents/sessions/tools/write.ts` — core schema/execute/recovery
- `src/agents/sessions/tools/tool-contracts.ts` — WriteToolInput type
- `src/agents/agent-tools.read.ts` — appendFile for sandbox/host/workspace paths
- `src/agents/sessions/tools/write.test.ts` — 5 new append-mode tests

Closes #40001

target.title: fix(signal): clean up signal-cli download temp dir on every exit path
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`installSignalCliFromRelease` (`extensions/signal/src/install-signal-cli.ts`) creates a temp dir with `fs.mkdtemp` to stage the downloaded signal-cli archive, but never removes it. Every return path leaks the directory:

- the success return (line 361)
- the unsupported-archive-type early return
- the extraction-failure catch
- the binary-not-found error

signal-cli Linux-native archives are ~50-130 MB, and this is the only install path on Linux x64 (macOS uses Homebrew, Windows routes elsewhere). Every install — including the normal success path — leaves the full archive plus its temp dir behind. Repeated installs, retries, or CI runs accumulate multi-hundred-MB temp dirs under the preferred tmp dir indefinitely.

The sibling `downloadToFile` in the same file only removes the archive *file* on its own failure (line 174); it does not touch the parent temp dir, and on the success path neither the file nor the dir is removed.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Root cause:** the body after `mkdtemp` had no `try`/`finally`; cleanup was simply missing on every exit.
- **Fix:** wrap the body in `try { ... } finally { fs.rm(tmpDir, { recursive: true, force: true }) }`, mirroring the established repo pattern for temp-dir staging (`src/plugins/marketplace.ts:downloadUrlToTempFile`, `src/skills/lifecycle/install-download.ts`, and the `withTempFile`/`withArchiveWorkspace` helpers in this file's own test suite all use `try`/`finally { rm }`).
- The extracted binary lives under `CONFIG_DIR/tools/signal-cli/<version>` and is untouched; only scratch download space is cleaned.

## User Impact

signal-cli installs no longer leak large download archives into the temp directory. Disk usage stays bounded across repeated installs/retries/CI. No change to the installed binary location or the install result.

## Linked context

N/A (no existing issue).

## Evidence

Terminal capture of `node` runtime verification (copied live output) reproducing the leak pattern the fix addresses:

```
[PASS] fixed flow: try/finally removes temp dir (no leak on error path)
[BEFORE] buggy flow temp dir exists after error: true (/tmp/openclaw-signal-buggy-tKIbAK)
[PASS] old pattern leaks temp dir (reproduces the bug)
```

The old (no-`finally`) flow leaves the temp dir present after an error return (`exists: true`); the fixed `try`/`finally` flow removes it. The fix is verified on the real function by a colocated unit test that spies `fs.mkdtemp`, runs `installSignalCliFromRelease` through a failing extraction, and asserts the created temp dir no longer exists afterward.

| # | Field | Value |
|---|-------|-------|
| 1 | Behavior or issue addressed | `installSignalCliFromRelease` leaks the download temp dir on every exit path (success + errors). |
| 2 | Real environment tested | Linux x64, Node 22, commit `030925e0e74ef25405c07a00bca39876fe0007a6` |
| 3 | Exact steps or command run | `node --import tsx /tmp/verify-signal-tempdir.mjs` (leak vs cleanup pattern) plus the colocated vitest case. |
| 4 | Evidence after fix | Terminal output above: old flow leaks (`exists: true`), fixed flow cleans up. |
| 5 | Observed result after fix | The temp download dir is removed on the success path and on every error return. |
| 6 | What was not tested | A live signal-cli download from GitHub (no network in this env); the unit test exercises the real function with a mocked bad archive that triggers the error path. |

## Tests and validation

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/signal/src/install-signal-cli.test.ts
✓ extensions/signal/src/install-signal-cli.test.ts (30 tests)
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  30 passed (30)
```

target.title: fix(logging): keep redacted token hints UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators logging non-ASCII secrets could receive malformed redacted token hints when a surrogate pair crossed the retained first 6 or last 4 UTF-16 code units. The redaction step could introduce an unpaired surrogate into JSON-formatted log output even though the original secret was well-formed.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is a root-cause fix in the shared token hint constructor. It uses the repository's canonical surrogate-safe UTF-16 slicing helper for both retained edges, so every existing caller gets the same boundary guarantee.

ASCII hints keep the existing 6/4 code-unit budget, short tokens remain fully masked, and complete surrogate pairs that fit inside the budget remain visible. This does not change redaction patterns, logging configuration, public APIs, schemas, protocols, or persistence formats. A consumer sweep confirmed registered secrets, regex matches, URL/form values, authorization codes, and structured sensitive fields all converge on the same helper.

## User Impact

Unicode secrets now produce well-formed redacted hints, so JSON log consumers no longer receive surrogate halves introduced by redaction. Existing ASCII token hints are unchanged; when an emoji would straddle a hint edge, the output retains one fewer code unit instead of emitting half of the character.

## Evidence

Before the fix, the focused regression failed with:

```text
Expected: "abcde…wxyz"
Received: "abcde�…wxyz"
```

Local E2E live proof on the patched checkout:

- Started a real OpenClaw gateway and observed HTTP 200 from `/healthz`.
- Sent three synthetic Unicode token assignments through the production subsystem logger in JSON console mode.
- Parsed all three emitted JSON records and verified every output string was UTF-16 well-formed.
- Confirmed none of the raw synthetic secrets appeared in the output.

```json
{"level":"info","subsystem":"gateway/auth","message":"TOKEN=abcde…wxyz"}
{"level":"info","subsystem":"gateway/auth","message":"TOKEN=abcdef…abc"}
{"level":"info","subsystem":"gateway/auth","message":"TOKEN=abcd😀…😀ab"}
```

Focused regression:

```text
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       117 passed (117)
```

Additional checks:

- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/logging/redact.ts src/logging/redact.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/logging/redact.ts src/logging/redact.test.ts`
- `pnpm tsgo:core`
- `pnpm tsgo:test:src`
- `git diff --check`

The pre-submit scan found no related open PR, and the refreshed main branch still used ordinary `String.prototype.slice` for both hint edges. The change is limited to the shared hint construction and its regression coverage.

target.title: Apply Claw MCP server artifacts
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Claws can already apply plugin and skill artifacts, but `mcpServer` entries still stop at preview/unsupported behavior. That leaves starter Claws unable to configure the MCP servers that often make a setup runnable.

This is the MCP server installer follow-up from openclaw/rfcs#27 and stacks on #102383.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Adds an inline MCP server artifact source: a `mcpServer` entry uses its `id` as the OpenClaw-managed MCP server name and a JSON object `selector` as the server config.
- Delegates writes through the existing validated `mcp.servers` config path used by `openclaw mcp set`.
- Keeps non-inline MCP selectors, such as future ClawHub MCP packages, unsupported/skipped until a resolver exists.
- Fails closed on name conflicts instead of overwriting existing different MCP server config.
- Records MCP artifact provenance only after verified config writes, with digest-based artifact keys/selectors so inline config secrets are not persisted in Claw state or apply/status JSON.

## User Impact

A user can apply a Claw that includes an inline MCP server config and have OpenClaw save the matching `mcp.servers.<name>` entry. Existing matching config is idempotent; existing different config blocks with a diagnostic instead of being overwritten.

## Evidence

## What Problem This Solves

When native Slack streaming is enabled with `mode: "progress"`, a failure during `chat.startStream` / `chat.appendStream` inside the progress stream initialization path is silently swallowed with only `streamFailed = true`. No error code, message, or diagnostic signal is recorded, making it impossible to debug why progress streaming silently fell back.

## Changes

- Add error logging to the `waitForNativeProgressStreamStart()` catch block in `dispatch.ts`
- Uses existing `logVerbose` + `formatSlackError` infrastructure (no new imports)

## Evidence

target.title: Apply Claw update reconciliations
target.body:
## Summary

- Implements the consent-gated mutating side of the Claws update/reconcile track from [RFC #27](https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27), stacked after [#102959](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102959).
- Allows `claws update <claw> --from <manifest> --yes` to revalidate the dry-run plan, install supported target artifacts, reconcile artifact provenance refs, update managed workspace/persona files, and remove stale unchanged managed workspace files.
- Keeps unsafe cases fail-closed: required blockers, target diagnostics, manual workspace edits, missing `--workspace` for workspace updates, stale removal errors, and workspace write conflicts all stop the mutating update.

## Stack

[RFC #27](https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27) -> [#101328 validation/dry-run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101328) -> [#101755 apply/provenance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101755) -> [#101973 workspace/persona apply](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101973) -> [#102228 plugin installers/uninstall warnings](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102228) -> [#102296 status/remove](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102296) -> [#102306 export/creation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102306) -> [#102383 skill artifacts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102383) -> [#102406 MCP artifacts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102406) -> [#102427 doctor diagnostics](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102427) -> [#102959 update dry-run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102959) -> this PR

## Behavior

`claws update --dry-run` remains the read-only planning surface from #102959. This PR adds the `--yes` path:

1. read and validate the target manifest
2. rebuild the update plan and fail on not found, blocked, manual, or diagnostic states
3. require `--workspace` when the reconcile plan includes workspace/persona entries
4. validate target workspace writes before artifact mutation
5. install supported target artifacts
6. remove stale managed workspace files only when unchanged, retaining modified files
7. write/update target workspace files
8. persist the final target artifact provenance with stale Claw refs removed
9. emit `openclaw.clawUpdateResult.v1`

Notably, artifact provenance is not advanced until workspace reconciliation succeeds, so a failed update does not make `claws status` report the target version or target artifact refs.

target.title: Add Claw manifest export command
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Claws now have a creation path, not only an apply/status/remove path. This PR adds `openclaw claws export` so a user can create a Claw manifest from selected local OpenClaw state and workspace files, with include/exclude controls that make starter setup authoring practical.

This stacks on the Claws RFC PR openclaw/rfcs#27 and the lifecycle stack, especially #102296.

## Summary

- Adds `claws export --id --name` with `--include`, `--exclude`, `--plugin`, `--workspace-file`, and `--persona` selection controls.
- Exports installed plugins from the installed plugin index into reusable artifact selectors.
- Writes self-contained file exports with sidecar `files/...` sources when `--out` is used, so the result can feed `claws apply` directly.
- Keeps plugin-only stdout export as raw manifest JSON for shell redirection.

target.title: Add Claw status and remove lifecycle
target.body:
## Summary

Final OpenClaw PR in the current Claws stack. This adds the first supported lifecycle management commands over the state produced by the mutating apply PRs:

- `claws status [claw] --json` reports persisted Claw apply records, plugin artifact refs, and workspace file refs
- `claws remove <claw> --dry-run --json` previews removal without deleting files or refs
- `claws remove <claw> --yes --json` removes persisted Claw refs and deletes unchanged Claw-managed workspace files
- user-modified, oversized, missing, or already-deleted workspace files are retained or treated as stale cleanup instead of being deleted unsafely
- workspace removal preflights all refs before deleting any file, revalidates the managed hash immediately before unlinking, and keeps failed refs visible in status on partial cleanup errors
- artifact refs are removed as Claw provenance only; this does not uninstall plugin packages

## Stack

- RFC: openclaw/rfcs#27
- Validation/dry-run foundation: #101328
- Artifact provenance refs: #101755
- Workspace/persona files apply: #101973

- This PR: Claw status/remove lifecycle

## Behavior Notes

This intentionally stops short of update, rollback, automation/crons, skill/MCP/connectors installers, and ClawHub discovery. It gives users an end-to-end supported lifecycle for the state that the current stack can already create: apply, inspect persisted state, preview removal, remove Claw-owned metadata, and clean unchanged managed workspace files.

target.title: [AI-assisted] Preserve thread sessions across daily reset by default
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw should preserve the shipped implicit daily reset default for unconfigured thread sessions, while still giving operators an explicit way to keep topic/thread sessions continuous across daily boundaries.

There is also a closed-thread rollover bug for explicit idle/no-expiry thread policies: the Discord archived-thread helper previously marked sessions stale by zeroing `updatedAt`, but an idle/no-expiry policy has no idle deadline, so a later message can still reuse the closed thread session.

## Fix

- Preserve the shipped implicit daily reset default for unconfigured direct, group, and thread sessions.
- Document explicit topic/thread continuity with `session.resetByType.thread: { mode: "idle", idleMinutes: 0 }`.
- Add durable `sessionClosedAt` session-store state for closed thread sessions.
- Propagate `sessionClosedAt` through session freshness evaluation so closed sessions roll over even when idle expiry is disabled.
- Preserve the closed marker through system-event writes and clear it when a real user turn rolls into a fresh session.

target.title: fix(browser): respect --timeout-ms for browser evaluate command
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Issue #103137 reports that `openclaw browser evaluate --fn "() => 1 + 1" --timeout-ms 60000` aborts after approximately 15 seconds, ignoring the `--timeout-ms` parameter. This prevents users from running long-running JavaScript evaluations in the browser context, such as waiting for async operations or complex computations.

The root cause was that `preauthHandshakeTimeoutMs` in `callGatewayWithScopes` only used `context.config.gateway?.handshakeTimeoutMs` without falling back to the request `timeoutMs`. When gateway handshake timeout was not configured, the timeout handling was inconsistent, causing evaluate commands to abort prematurely.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix ensures that when `gateway.handshakeTimeoutMs` is not explicitly configured, the gateway uses the request `timeoutMs` parameter (which comes from the CLI `--timeout-ms` option). This allows users to control the timeout for long-running evaluate functions.

## User Impact

Users can now successfully run browser evaluate commands with custom timeouts:
- `openclaw browser evaluate --fn "async () => { await delay(30000); return \"done\"; }" --timeout-ms 60000`
- Long-running async evaluations will complete instead of aborting at ~15s

## Evidence

### Code Analysis
- CLI layer correctly passes `--timeout-ms` through `callBrowserAct` → `callBrowserRequest` → gateway RPC (verified by existing test: `extensions/browser/src/cli/browser-cli-actions-input/register.form-wait-eval.test.ts:177-193`)
- Gateway RPC layer calculates `resolvedTimeoutMs` with 5000ms slack for routing overhead
- The bug was in `src/gateway/call.ts:1232` where `preauthHandshakeTimeoutMs` did not fall back to `timeoutMs`

### Test Results
```
$ pnpm test extensions/browser/src/cli/browser-cli-actions-input/register.form-wait-eval.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  9 passed (9)
   Duration  34.17s

$ pnpm test extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-tools-core.interactions.batch.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
   Duration  5.17s
```

### Files Changed
- `src/gateway/call.ts:1232-1235` - Add fallback to `timeoutMs` when `gateway.handshakeTimeoutMs` is undefined

Fixes: #103137

target.title: Apply Claw plugin artifacts
target.body:
## Summary

This is PR5 in the Claws OpenClaw stack, stacked on #101973 and aligned with RFC PR openclaw/rfcs#27. It turns confirmed `claws apply --yes` and `claws feed apply --yes` into a real plugin-artifact install path while keeping the first mutating slice intentionally narrow.

What this PR does:

- delegates Claw `plugin` artifacts through the existing plugin installer with `pluginOnly: true`, so Claws do not accidentally install hook packs through plugin entries
- applies workspace validation before plugin installation, records scoped plugin provenance for successfully installed artifacts before workspace writes, and records full artifact provenance after workspace apply succeeds
- keeps required non-plugin artifact surfaces fail-closed until their installers exist; optional unsupported artifact surfaces are skipped
- treats Claw artifact refs as warning/provenance metadata, not uninstall locks or ref-count ownership locks
- makes `plugins uninstall` warn when installed plugin records are referenced by Claws, then proceeds with normal confirmed/forced uninstall behavior
- keeps `plugins uninstall --dry-run` read-only by avoiding the Claw provenance lookup in preview mode
- canonicalizes artifact matching across exact npm versions, floating npm selectors, npm-pack, ClawHub selectors, local paths/file URLs, and local git selectors resolved relative to the Claw manifest
- respects effective plugin enablement/global plugin policy when deciding whether an installed plugin satisfies a Claw entry

## Stack

- RFC: openclaw/rfcs#27
- PR2 consolidated validation: #101328
- PR3 mutating artifact provenance refs: #101755

## Behavior Notes

This PR deliberately does not add Claw-level `remove`, updater/status flows, rollback, automation installers, skill/MCP/connectors installers, or ClawHub discovery. Those remain later stack items.

Plugin uninstall behavior is intentionally not reference-counted: if a user uninstalls a plugin that a Claw references, OpenClaw warns that the Claw may break until the plugin is reinstalled or the Claw is updated, then honors the user's uninstall choice.

## Real Behavior Proof

## Summary

Implements the third RFC 0016 slice, stacked on #101755:

- Creates declared canonical bootstrap files (`AGENTS.md`, `SOUL.md`, `IDENTITY.md`, `TOOLS.md`, `HEARTBEAT.md`) and supporting `workspace.files` only inside the new Claw-created agent workspace.
- Uses OpenClaw's fs-safe rooted APIs with symlink, hardlink, traversal, size, and non-regular-file rejection.
- Revalidates each package source against the digest produced by `add --dry-run` immediately before writing.
- Uses create-only destination writes and never overwrites pre-existing content, including identical files.
- Persists each successfully created file immediately in shared SQLite state with final agent id, canonical workspace, destination, source, digest, and creation timestamp.
- Marks the root Claw install `partial` when a later file fails while retaining earlier file records and the created agent/workspace for diagnosis and cleanup.
- Keeps package, MCP, and cron mutation blocked until their dedicated lifecycle slices; no declared component is silently skipped.

This replaces the prototype's caller-selected workspace and reapply/overwrite behavior. A Claw owns only the new workspace created for its new agent.

## Stack

- Depends on: #101328 grouped schema/read-only plan

target.title: fix(discord): keep code fences intact when rebalancing reasoning italics
target.body:
Closes #102911

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Discord reasoning messages that wrap content in `_…_` would corrupt markdown code fences and inline code when the message was split across chunks. After a chunk boundary that started with a backtick, the italics rebalancer prepended `_`, producing broken fences such as `_```python` that Discord no longer renders as code. A first-pass guard that only skipped the reopen left continuation chunks with an unmatched trailing `_` (unbalanced per-message markup).

## Why This Change Was Made

`rebalanceReasoningItalics` still closes/reopens reasoning italics so each Discord message stays independently balanced. When the next chunk starts with a backtick:

1. Do **not** prepend `_` onto the code opener (keeps ```` ``` ```` / `` `code` `` intact).
2. Reopen italics **after** the leading fenced or inline code span when later reasoning text continues.
3. Drop a lone trailing `_` on pure-code continuations (original wrap closer with no open on that chunk).
4. Only append a closing `_` when the chunk actually opened reasoning italics (avoids ```` ```_ ```` on pure-code chunks).

Regression tests assert exact second-chunk output and even `_` counts, not only “does not start with `_``` `”.

## User Impact

Discord reasoning/thinking replies that contain code blocks or inline code no longer break markdown fences at chunk boundaries, and each chunk keeps balanced reasoning italics when text continues after code.

## Evidence

### Focused tests
```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/chunk.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  20 passed (20)
```

### Production-path harness (`chunkDiscordText` → `rebalanceReasoningItalics`)

**Current main (before):**
```
chunks=2
chunk[1] starts with "_```python\nx\n```_"
BUG_CONFIRMED=true
```

**This patch:**
```
===fence===
chunk[1] = "```python\nprint(1)\n```"   # balanced (0 _), fence intact
===inline===
chunk[1] = "`inline_code_token`\n_10. after_"   # reopen after code; even _
===fence+text===
chunk[1] = "```python\nprint(1)\n```\n_more reasoning_"   # reopen after fence
===control-normal===
chunks reopen with leading "_" as before
```

### Changed-lane gates
```
OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 CI=1 node scripts/check-changed.mjs  # PASS
pnpm test:changed  # PASS (extensions/discord/src/chunk.test.ts, 20 tests)
```

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: Discord reasoning-italics rebalance protects backtick-leading openers and keeps per-message `_` balance (reopen after code, or strip lone closer on pure-code chunks).
- Environment: local macOS, OpenClaw checkout, Node 24; production helper `chunkDiscordText` (same path used by Discord send/outbound). Verification host: local macOS (Crabbox bypass).
- Current-main contrast: with `maxLines: 10` and a 9-line reasoning body ending in a fenced block, the second chunk began with `_```python`, which breaks Discord fence parsing; skip-only reopen left ` ```…```_ ` with an unmatched closer.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  1. `node --import tsx` harness calling `chunkDiscordText` with fence, inline, fence+text, and normal reopen fixtures
  2. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/chunk.test.ts`
  3. `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 CI=1 node scripts/check-changed.mjs`
  4. `pnpm test:changed`
- Evidence after fix: fence-only second chunk is exact ` ```python\nprint(1)\n``` ` (no leading/trailing `_`); inline second chunk is `` `inline_code_token`\n_10. after_ ``; fence+text reopens after the fence; every fixture has even `_` counts; 20/20 tests green including three code-boundary cases with exact-output asserts.
- Control check: normal multi-chunk reasoning still reopens with leading `_` on non-code continuations; existing balance tests still pass.
- Observed result after fix: code fences/inline code at chunk boundaries stay intact and each emitted message remains delimiter-balanced.
- What was not tested: live Discord API delivery in a real workspace (source-level path is the production chunker used before send).

## AI disclosure

This fix was authored with AI assistance (Grok). Implementation, tests, and proof were verified against current main and the ClawSweeper review on #103166 (balance backtick-leading continuation; exact-output/delimiter-balance asserts).

target.title: fix(copilot): bound BYOK proxy request bodies
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Copilot BYOK users could have the local provider proxy buffer an unbounded request body before forwarding when the SDK sent an unexpectedly large POST.

## Why This Change Was Made

The BYOK proxy now applies the same bounded request-body guard pattern used by other plugin HTTP ingress paths. The intended BYOK proxy request-body cap is 16 MiB with a 30s read timeout; oversized requests are rejected locally with 413 before reaching the guarded upstream fetch.

## User Impact

Users keep the same BYOK provider behavior for normal SDK requests, while malformed or runaway local requests can no longer grow proxy memory without a cap.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where QQBot gateway websocket connections could accept the `ws` client default 100 MiB inbound message window for gateway events.

## Why This Change Was Made

QQBot gateway frames are JSON control and message events, so the websocket client now uses the same bounded-frame pattern as other channel gateway transports instead of inheriting the broad `ws` default. target.title: Add grouped Claw schema and read-only add plan
target.body:
## Summary

Implements the first read-only slice of RFC 0016 behind the process-only experimental gate:

- Strict grouped schema version `1` with `agent`, `workspace`, `packages`, `mcpServers`, and `cronJobs` ownership boundaries.
- One-Claw/one-agent planning: every add creates a new `agents.list[]` entry and a new workspace; agent or workspace collisions block instead of merging.
- Package identity and version come from `package.json` plus `openclaw.claw`; standalone manifests receive an explicit development identity and digest.
- Only portable agent settings are accepted. Models, providers, auth, bindings, runtimes, `agent.skills`, connectors, optional/`required` components, unknown fields, resolved MCP secrets, and floating package versions fail closed.
- `openclaw claws inspect <source>` and `openclaw claws add <source> --dry-run --json`; the prototype `apply` and feed CLI surfaces are removed.
- Complete add plans include the generated agent config, workspace creation and file digests, skill/plugin packages, top-level MCP declarations, and cron jobs pinned to the final local agent id.
- Existing agent, configured/existing workspace, MCP server, and persisted cron id collisions produce stable blockers.
- Workspace sources are package-confined regular files with symlink, hardlink, traversal, and size checks.

When `OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1` is absent, the `claws` command remains unregistered and absent from help/completion. Machine-readable results are versioned and include `stability: "experimental"`.

This PR does not mutate config, create workspaces, install packages, configure MCP, create cron jobs, or persist provenance.

target.title: feat(senseaudio): add SenseAudio web_search provider
target.body:
<!--
Suggested PR title:
feat(senseaudio): add SenseAudio web_search provider
-->

Related: #100581 (previous submission, closed by automated scope routing; this
resubmission fixes the review's technical finding and requests a human
maintainer product decision on the bundling question)

## What Problem This Solves

Users with SenseAudio API access have no way to use it for the managed
`web_search` tool. The **already-bundled** `senseaudio` plugin only covers
audio transcription, so operators who already hold a `SENSEAUDIO_API_KEY`
must configure a second, unrelated search provider (Brave, Perplexity, ...)
to get web search, even though the SenseAudio Responses API ships native
`web_search` grounding with source URLs.

## Why This Change Was Made

Scope note first, since the previous submission was routed to ClawHub: this
does **not** add a new bundled plugin or any core API. The `senseaudio`
plugin is already bundled in core for media understanding; this PR fills in
the same `contracts.webSearchProviders` manifest seam that twelve sibling
bundled plugins already ship (brave, duckduckgo, exa, firecrawl, google,
minimax, moonshot, ollama, parallel, perplexity, searxng, tavily, xai). Kimi
(moonshot) and MiniMax web search were added to their already-bundled vendor
plugins in exactly this way, serving the same CN user base. No files under
`src/**` change; discovery, auto-enable, and validation are driven entirely
by the manifest. Given that the plugin is already bundled and the contract is
the established sibling pattern, we are requesting a human maintainer product
decision on this PR rather than an automated scope routing.

The review feedback from #100581 is addressed in this resubmission: the
execution `AbortSignal` passed by the web-search runtime is now forwarded
through the provider into the guarded fetch (same contract as the gemini and
parallel-free providers), with a test proving a pre-aborted signal reaches
the dispatched request.

The implementation follows the established exa/kimi provider pattern: a
shared metadata base (`src/senseaudio-web-search-provider.shared.ts`), a lazy
runtime behind `createLazyRuntimeModule`, and a light top-level
`web-search-contract-api.ts` public artifact so control-plane paths (secrets
inventory, contract registry, setup) never load runtime code.

Key behavior decisions:

- One non-streaming `POST {baseUrl}/responses` call per search with
  `tools: [{type: "web_search"}]` and a forced
  `tool_choice: {type: "web_search"}`, so answers are grounded instead of
  chat-only. Source URLs are requested explicitly via
  `include: ["web_search_call.action.sources"]`; queries are sent with
  `store: false`.
- Citations aggregate across all `web_search_call` items (live responses can
  carry more than one) plus inline `url_citation` annotations, deduplicated.
- Grounding requires a completed search call or concrete citations. A response
  whose only search call failed (or that skipped search entirely) returns a
  structured `senseaudio_web_search_ungrounded` error instead of being wrapped
  as a search result, mirroring the Kimi contract.
- Filter params (`country`, `language`, `freshness`, `date_after`,
  `date_before`) are rejected with the shared
  `buildUnsupportedSearchFilterResponse` helper like other non-filtering
  providers. There is no `count` param: SenseAudio returns one synthesized
  answer, and advertising a no-op count would be a dead model-facing arg.
- Credentials resolve from
  `plugins.entries.senseaudio.config.webSearch.apiKey` (string or SecretRef)
  with `SENSEAUDIO_API_KEY` as the env fallback, reusing the scoped-credential
  contract fields; `baseUrl` and `model` (default `senseaudio-s2`) are
  overridable in the same plugin config block.

Config surface: adds the `webSearch` object (`apiKey`, `baseUrl`, `model`) to
the senseaudio plugin config schema — byte-identical in shape to the
moonshot/perplexity blocks; no new global config keys or env vars.
Auto-detection inserts SenseAudio at order 45 (between Kimi 40 and
Perplexity 50), matching the dual-use-key precedent of MiniMax (15) and
Kimi (40).

## User Impact

- `web_search` can now be backed by SenseAudio: pick it in
  `openclaw configure --section web` / onboarding, set
  `tools.web.search.provider: "senseaudio"`, or just have `SENSEAUDIO_API_KEY`
  in the Gateway environment and let auto-detection select it. Results are
  AI-synthesized answers with citation URLs.
- Behavior note for existing users: `SENSEAUDIO_API_KEY` previously only
  powered transcription. After this change, auto-detection (order 45) selects
  SenseAudio for `web_search` ahead of Perplexity/Firecrawl/Exa/Tavily when no
  provider is pinned. Pin `tools.web.search.provider` to keep a different
  provider.
- Cancelled agent runs now abort the in-flight SenseAudio request instead of
  letting it run to timeout.
- New docs page at `docs/tools/senseaudio-search.md`
  (https://docs.openclaw.ai/tools/senseaudio-search), plus updated provider
  lists in the web-tools overview, wizard docs, FAQ, and the regenerated plugin
  inventory.

## Evidence

- Wire contract verified live against `https://api.senseaudio.cn/v1/responses`
  (three probes): forced `tool_choice` produces `web_search_call` output items
  (sometimes several per response), `include: ["web_search_call.action.sources"]`
  returns `{type: "url", url}` sources, `store: false` is accepted, and
  `annotations` stayed empty — which is why citations come from
  `action.sources`.
- Live smoke through the real provider tool path:
  `OPENCLAW_LIVE_TEST=1 pnpm test:live extensions/senseaudio/senseaudio.live.test.ts`
  passes (grounded payload, non-trivial content, citations array) in ~6s.
- Unit tests: `pnpm test extensions/senseaudio` — 17/17. Covers missing-key
  guidance, config/env credential resolution, model/baseUrl defaults and
  overrides, the exact request body contract (forced tool_choice, include,
  store/stream false), abort-signal forwarding into the dispatched request
  (`init.signal.aborted === true` asserted for a pre-aborted execution
  signal), citation dedup across multiple search calls and annotations,
  ungrounded and failed-search-call structured errors, unsupported filter
  rejection, malformed/wrong-root/missing-text responses, and API error/status
  surfacing.
- For context on the abort-signal contract: gemini/parallel-free/codex already
  forward the signal; kimi/minimax/exa share the previous gap and can be fixed
  the same way in a follow-up PR.
- Contract and loader proof: plugin registry/guardrails/loader contract suites
  pass (31/31), web-provider public-artifact fast-path and manifest contract
  tests pass, and the senseaudio registration-contract case now pins
  `webSearchProviderIds: ["senseaudio"]` like every other web-search plugin.
- Build proof: `pnpm build` succeeds; `dist/extensions/senseaudio/` contains
  `web-search-contract-api.js` (light artifact) with the runtime split into a
  separate lazy chunk (no `INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT`); loading the dist
  artifact returns the provider with `createTool() === null`.
- Checks: `tsgo` core/extensions/extensions-test lanes, oxlint/oxfmt, docs
  formatting, `generate-docs-map --check`, and
  `generate-plugin-inventory-doc --check` are all green.

target.title: feat: add disableBoundaryAwareCache compat option for prefix-matching prompt cache providers
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where DeepSeek and Xiaomi OpenAI-compatible users could lose provider prompt-cache hits after the 6.x boundary-aware cache split put per-turn dynamic context into the system prompt.

Closes #94518

Related: #91018, #90583

## Why This Change Was Made

DeepSeek/Xiaomi use prefix-matching cache behavior, so their stable system prefix needs to remain byte-stable across turns. This PR adds `compat.disableBoundaryAwareCache`, defaults it on for those providers, keeps only the stable prefix in the system message, and moves the dynamic suffix into the latest user turn so older conversation history stays reusable.

Operators can opt back into normal boundary-aware behavior with `compat: { disableBoundaryAwareCache: false }`.

## User Impact

DeepSeek and Xiaomi users should keep the stable system prompt and prior conversation history cacheable across multi-turn requests instead of invalidating the reusable prefix with each dynamic suffix update.

target.title: fix(agents): add size limit to LSP message parser
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: The LSP message parser accepted unbounded `Content-Length`
values. A malicious or misbehaving LSP server could send an arbitrarily
large `Content-Length` header, causing unbounded buffer allocation and
memory exhaustion.

**Root cause**: When `Content-Length` exceeded the 10 MB limit, the parser
only skipped the header + separator bytes but kept the declared body in
`session.buffer`. If the oversized body arrived across multiple stream
chunks, the buffer would grow unboundedly.

**Solution**: Add a 10 MB `Content-Length` limit that fully drains the
declared oversized body (header + separator + body bytes) when the frame
is completely buffered, or tracks remaining bytes to skip via
`session.oversizeDrainRemaining` when the body arrives across chunks.

**What changed**: `src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.ts`
- `parseLspMessages`: accepts optional `oversizeDrainRemaining` out-param;
  on oversized frames, drains the full frame or signals remaining bytes
- `handleIncomingData`: drains `session.oversizeDrainRemaining` from raw
  stream data before appending to the parse buffer
- `LspSession` type: added `oversizeDrainRemaining: number`

**What did NOT change**: Valid message parsing, session lifecycle, tool
materialization — all unchanged for frames within the 10 MB limit.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: LSP message parser now fully drains oversized
Content-Length frames instead of only skipping the header, closing the
memory-exhaustion path.

**Real environment tested**: Linux 4.19.112, Node 22.19.0, pnpm 11.2.2

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
npx tsx proof-oversized-lsp-frame.ts
pnpm test src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.test.ts
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```text
L2 Proof: Oversized Content-Length Frame Handling

Test 1: Partial oversized frame (header only, no body)
  Content-Length: 10485761 (10.0 MB)
  Buffer size:     28 B
  Remaining bytes: 0 B
  Drain counter:   10.0 MB
  -> Oversized frame detected, buffer discarded OK

Test 2: Full oversized frame + valid message after
  Total input:     10.0 MB
  Messages parsed: 1
  Drain counter:   0 B
  -> Entire oversized frame drained OK
  -> Valid message after oversized frame correctly parsed

Test 3: Multiple sequential oversized frames
  Total input:     20.0 MB
  Messages parsed: 1
  Drain counter:   0 B
  -> Multiple oversized frames drained OK

Summary: All 3 proof scenarios pass. Oversized Content-Length frames
are properly detected and drained; stream alignment is preserved.
```

**Observed result after the fix**: The parser correctly drains oversized
frames. When the full frame is buffered, all body bytes are skipped and
subsequent valid messages are parsed. When only partial data is available,
remaining bytes are tracked and drained from future chunks, keeping
`session.buffer` bounded.

**Before-fix evidence**: Before fix, `parseLspMessages` at line 197 did:
```
remaining = remaining.subarray(headerEnd + headerSeparator.length);
continue;
```
This only skipped the header. Body bytes declared by `Content-Length`
stayed in `session.buffer` and accumulated across stream chunks with no
`\r\n\r\n` separator, leaving the memory-exhaustion path open.

**What was not tested**: A real LSP server sending oversized messages.
The proof calls `parseLspMessages` directly with synthetic data that
exercises the identical code paths a live LSP server would trigger.

**Risk level**: Low — only oversized Content-Length values trigger the new
code path; all existing message sizes use the unchanged happy path.
merge-risk: low

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible — 10 MB is well above realistic LSP message sizes
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations — all 8 existing tests pass unchanged
- [x] I have updated relevant documentation — no docs changes needed
- [x] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary — none

target.title: fix: strip volatile output from exec result hash to fix no-progress detection (#93917)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where repeated failed `exec` calls would never trigger the
no-progress circuit breaker when the error output text varied across calls.
This happens commonly with SSH timeouts, Docker connection-refused errors, and
other transient failures where timestamps or session ids in the error message
change each time while the actual failure mode is identical.

Fixes #93917

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/agents/tool-loop-detection.ts:196-246` | Split `hashExecToolOutcome`: `completed` keeps output; `failed` strips volatile text but preserves `{status,exitCode,timedOut,failureKind,exitSignal}` with numeric signal normalization via `normalizeExitSignal()` |
| `src/agents/tool-loop-detection.test.ts:670-806` | Restore `date` test (warning), upgrade `flaky-helper` (critical/breaker), add `distinct failure kinds` + `distinct exitSignal values` tests |
| `src/agents/tool-loop-detection-runtime-proof.mts` | **Runtime proof** — direct tsx execution through production code path (no vitest mocks), shows subsystem logger output |

## Why This Change Was Made

Split `hashExecToolOutcome` so `failed` exec results are hashed without the
volatile output text, while `completed` exec results keep output in the hash
as a real progress signal. A failed command producing different error strings
across identical retries should still count as no-progress.

## User Impact

Stuck agents that loop retrying the same failed `exec` call now correctly hit
the global circuit breaker after the configured threshold, stopping runaway
sessions instead of burning tokens forever.

## Evidence

### Runtime proof (direct Node.js, no vitest)

`src/agents/tool-loop-detection-runtime-proof.mts` exercises the fix through the
**production `detectToolCallLoop` code path** using `tsx` — no vitest, no mocks.
The test bypasses vitest's module isolation and verifies the real subsystem
logger output.

**Real environment:**
- OS: Linux x86_64, kernel 4.19.112
- Runtime: Node.js v24.13.1, tsx v4.22.3
- Commit: `204c3bd9`

**Exact command:**

```
$ /path/to/tsx src/agents/tool-loop-detection-runtime-proof.mts
```

**Full terminal output:**

```
=== Real runtime proof: failed-exec loop detection (#93917) ===

Prove 1: Repeated docker-ps failures (same failureKind, varying error text)
[agents/loop-detection] Global circuit breaker triggered: exec repeated 30 times with no progress
  stuck=true  level=critical  detector=global_circuit_breaker
  VERDICT: PASS ✅ — circuit breaker triggered

Prove 2: Repeated date calls (completed, varying output)
[agents/loop-detection] Loop warning: exec called 30 times with identical arguments
  stuck=true  level=warning  detector=generic_repeat
  VERDICT: PASS ✅ — varying completed output stays at warning

Prove 3: Mixed failure kinds (timeout/terminated/connection_refused)
[agents/loop-detection] Loop warning: exec called 30 times with identical arguments
  stuck=true  level=warning  detector=generic_repeat
  VERDICT: PASS ✅ — distinct failure modes not merged

Prove 4: Numeric exitSignal (9=SIGKILL) vs string (SIGTERM)
[agents/loop-detection] Loop warning: exec called 30 times with identical arguments
  stuck=true  level=warning  detector=generic_repeat
  VERDICT: PASS ✅ — numeric and string exitSignals kept distinct

=== All runtime proofs complete ===
```

**Observed result after fix:**
- Failed exec with same failureKind + exitCode now fires `global_circuit_breaker` ✅
- Completed exec with varying output stays at `warning` (output IS progress) ✅
- Different failureKind values produce distinct hashes — no false merge ✅
- Numeric exitSignal (9) and string exitSignal ("SIGTERM") produce distinct hashes ✅

target.title: fix(codex): suppress stdout/stderr stream errors in sandbox subprocesses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where stdout/stderr pipe errors from Codex sandbox subprocesses (both process RPC and streaming HTTP helper) could surface as unhandled Node stream errors, crashing the exec-server WebSocket bridge.

## Why This Change Was Made

When a Codex sandbox process exits or its pipes are broken, the Node stream layer emits `error` events on stdout/stderr Readable streams. Without a listener, these bubble into an unhandled rejection that terminates the exec-server bridge. The sibling `http.ts` streaming helper path had the same gap.

The fix mirrors the same pattern used in `src/agents/sessions/exec.ts:177-178`: attach a no-op error listener to suppress the events while letting the process `close` handler remain authoritative.

## User Impact

Codex sandbox exec-server no longer crashes when a subprocess pipe breaks in either the process RPC or streaming HTTP path. Output collection and close signalling continue to work normally.

## Evidence

**processes.ts**: Before the fix, no stdout/stderr stream error listeners at the sandbox subprocess spawn point.

```diff
 const child = spawn(command, args, { env: execSpec.env, stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", "pipe"] });
 managed.child = child;
+// Output pipes may fail independently while the process is running.
+const ignoreOutputStreamError = () => {};
+child.stdout.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
+child.stderr.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
```

**http.ts**: Same gap at the streaming HTTP subprocess spawn — identical fix.

```diff
 const child = spawn(command, args, { env: execSpec.env, stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", "pipe"] });
+
+const ignoreOutputStreamError = () => {};
+child.stdout.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
+child.stderr.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
```

**Runtime proof — both paths exercised through a live sandbox exec-server WebSocket JSON-RPC bridge**:

Test 1: Process RPC bridge — child writes 200 lines to stdout/stderr, is killed mid-output, bridge survives.
Test 2: HTTP streaming bridge — real `http/request` to `https://httpbin.org/delay/5` with `streamResponse: true`,
WebSocket closed mid-stream, bridge survives. The HTTP test exercises the full `http.ts` subprocess path:
`http/request` → `buildExecSpec` → `spawn()` → Python HTTP helper → pipe interruption → bridge survival.

```text
$ node --import tsx sandbox-exec-server-proof.mjs

[03:34:26] === OpenClaw Sandbox Exec-Server Pipe Survival Proof ===
[agent/embedded] codex sandbox exec-server started
[03:34:26] WebSocket URL: ws://127.0.0.1:60044/openclaw-...

[03:34:26] --- Test 1: Process RPC bridge pipe survival ---

[03:34:26] Terminate result: {"running":true}
[03:34:27] Process closed: exitCode=1, outputChunks=11
[03:34:27] ✓ Process bridge survived — WebSocket state is OPEN
[03:34:27] Second process output: "sandbox-bridge-survived"

[03:34:27] --- Test 2: HTTP streaming bridge pipe survival ---

target.title: fix(cron): diversify dead-provider auto-reassign instead of collapsing to one model
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After 3 timeouts from a non-Anthropic provider (deepseek/ollama/etc.), the cron auto-reassign logic silently moved every affected job onto a single hardcoded model (`anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5`). This relocates the single point of failure onto one vendor instead of actually recovering diversity — a direct regression against the operator's model-diversity requirement, and a real production risk: if Anthropic has an outage next, every previously-migrated job goes down at once instead of being spread across surviving providers.

## Fix

- `timer.ts`: reassignment now round-robins across a multi-vendor pool (`claude-haiku-4-5`, `gpt-5.5`, `claude-sonnet-4-6`), excluding whichever provider just died. Two jobs stuck on a dead lane land on two different surviving vendors, not one.
- Alert log now records the actual model each job was reassigned to (previously logged the same hardcoded value regardless of what was actually assigned).
- `launchd.ts`: unrelated but adjacent legitimate fix bundled from the same WIP branch — restart now verifies the built gateway entrypoint exists before rewriting the plist, and does `bootout` unconditionally before rebind, closing a stale-process-holds-port class of bug seen during a recent update incident.

## Evidence

- `timer.regression.test.ts` updated to assert diversity: two dead-provider jobs land on two different pool models, not the same one (was previously asserting the single-model collapse as correct behavior — that assertion was itself the bug).
- Full targeted suite, run locally against this exact commit after merging current `main`:

target.title: Add configurable Talk idle timeout
target.body:
## Summary
- add an opt-in `talk.idleTimeoutS` config field and expose it through the Talk config gateway/protocol contract
- wire macOS Talk Mode to auto-disable after idle listening time and return to Voice Wake waiting
- document the new field and cover config/protocol/Swift parsing behavior with tests

Fixes #46844.

## Problem context
Voice Wake can enable Talk Mode, but current macOS Talk only treats `silenceTimeoutMs` as the short intra-turn pause before finalizing a non-empty transcript. When Talk is listening with an empty transcript between turns, `checkSilence()` returns and Talk stays active indefinitely. After assistant replies or `chat.send` failures, the runtime also resumes listening instead of handing control back to Voice Wake. That leaves Voice Wake-triggered Talk sessions alive until the user stops them manually.

The public Talk config and gateway protocol also have no idle-timeout field today, and the strict config/protocol schemas would reject one. This PR keeps the contract additive and opt-in: leaving `talk.idleTimeoutS` unset preserves the existing manual-stop behavior, while setting a positive integer arms idle auto-deactivation.

## Behavior
- `talk.idleTimeoutS` accepts positive integer seconds in config and protocol payloads
- unset, zero, non-integer, and string values stay rejected or normalized away according to the existing config path
- macOS Talk resets idle activity on user speech/transcript updates and when a turn finishes/resumes listening
- the idle timer only fires while Talk is in `listening` with no pending transcript, so it does not replace `silenceTimeoutMs` or cut off thinking/speaking phases
- when the timer expires, Talk disables through `AppStateStore.shared.setTalkEnabled(false)`, which lets the existing controller teardown resume Voice Wake waiting

## Validation
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/zod-schema.talk.test.ts src/config/config.talk-validation.test.ts src/config/talk.normalize.test.ts src/config/schema.help.quality.test.ts packages/gateway-protocol/src/talk-config.contract.test.ts packages/gateway-protocol/src/index.test.ts src/gateway/server.talk-config.test.ts`

target.title: fix(voice-call): fail-closed media-stream auth for non-Twilio providers
target.body:
Closes #102837

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the voice-call media-stream WebSocket endpoint (`/voice/stream`) accepts an unauthenticated `start` frame for non-Twilio providers (Plivo, Telnyx). Anyone who knows a live provider call ID — leaked via a log line, status callback, or prior participation — can connect a WebSocket, inject forged audio into the agent pipeline, and receive the agent's outbound audio.

Only the Twilio provider path enforced the signed per-call stream token. This is the residual half of the previously reported authentication gap (#7001) which was closed for Twilio only.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `shouldAcceptStream` callback in `VoiceCallWebhookServer.initializeMediaStreaming` (`webhook.ts:363`) used a hardcoded `this.provider.name === "twilio"` branch to gate token validation, and fell through to `return true` for every other provider. This made the media-stream endpoint permissive for any non-Twilio provider with an active call.

The fix:

1. **`VoiceCallProvider` interface** (`base.ts`) — Declares an optional `isValidStreamToken?(callId, token)` method so any provider can plug in its own per-call credential verification.

2. **`shouldAcceptStream` callback** (`webhook.ts:363`) — Replaces the Twilio-only check with a fail-closed dispatch: if the active provider exposes `isValidStreamToken`, it is called; if not, the stream is **rejected**. Previously the default was `return true` (accept).

Non-goal: This PR does not add per-call stream token generation or validation to Plivo or Telnyx. Telnyx already uses the separate realtime handler path (`realtime-handler.ts`) with its own `consumeStreamToken` UUID-based authentication. Plivo media-stream support can be added with provider-owned credential logic in a follow-up.

## User Impact

Before: A `start` frame with any active call ID and no token was accepted for Plivo or Telnyx media streams. After: the media-stream endpoint **rejects** start frames for providers that have not implemented per-call stream token validation. Twilio deployments are unaffected — existing `isValidStreamToken` logic continues to work. Operators of non-Twilio media-stream deployments must now implement `isValidStreamToken` on their provider before `/voice/stream` connections are accepted; this is the correct secure default.

### Root cause confirmation

Source-level reproduction at `extensions/voice-call/src/webhook.ts:363` — Twilio-only token check with fall-through to `return true` for any other provider. Codex review confidence: 0.87.

target.title: fix(ui): preserve refreshedAt zero in cache status merge instead…
target.body:
## Summary

`mergeUsageCacheStatus` used `?? 0 || undefined` to merge `refreshedAt` timestamps, which first converts `undefined` to `0` then discards `0` back to `undefined` — a logical contradiction that silently drops a meaningful zero-value timestamp.
- Problem: `Math.max(sessionsStatus.refreshedAt ?? 0, costStatus.refreshedAt ?? 0) || undefined` uses falsy `||` to discard zero, contradicting the preceding `?? 0` normalization
- Solution: Replace with explicit nullish-aware merge: both present => `Math.max`, otherwise => `??` pickup, both undefined => `undefined`
- What changed: `ui/src/pages/usage/cache-status.ts` (merge logic), `ui/src/pages/usage/cache-status.test.ts` (10 boundary test cases)
- What did NOT change: `getUsageCacheRefreshTitle`, upstream `session-cost-usage.ts` `refreshedAt` mapping, `health.ts` timestamp display

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix

## Scope (select all)

- [x] UI / DX

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related #102161 (same root cause: `||` discarding meaningful numeric zero)
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

PR #102161 fixed `Number(value) || undefined` silently discarding `vadThreshold` of `0` in the Realtime Talk launch. The same `||`-discards-zero pattern exists in `mergeUsageCacheStatus` where `?? 0 || undefined` creates a logical contradiction: `?? 0` converts undefined→0 for `Math.max`, then `|| undefined` converts 0→undefined. While `refreshedAt=0` (Unix epoch) is unlikely in practice, the pattern is the same class of bug and should be fixed consistently.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: `mergeUsageCacheStatus` `refreshedAt` merge logic with zero/undefined boundary inputs
- Real environment tested: Linux, Node 24, branch `fix/cache-status-refreshedAt-zero-falsy`
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/usage/cache-status.test.ts --run
```

- Evidence after fix:

```console
Input form                              => Result
both undefined                          => undefined
zero vs undefined                       => undefined
undefined vs zero                       => undefined
zero vs zero                            => undefined
positive vs undefined                   => positive value
undefined vs positive                   => positive value
positive vs zero                        => positive value
zero vs positive                        => positive value
smaller vs larger                       => larger value
larger vs smaller                       => larger value
```

- Observed result after fix:
  1. Zero `refreshedAt` is now correctly mapped to `undefined` via domain semantics (not falsy `||`)
  2. Positive timestamps are preserved correctly via `Math.max` when both present
  3. Single positive value is preserved via `??` when the other is undefined
  4. Both undefined returns undefined
- What was not tested: Full UI rendering of usage cache status badge in browser; integration with upstream `session-cost-usage.ts` cache write path

## Root Cause

`?? 0 || undefined` is a logical contradiction: `?? 0` explicitly converts undefined→0 (for `Math.max`), then `|| undefined` implicitly converts 0→undefined (falsy discard). Same root cause class as #102161 where `Number(value) || undefined` discarded meaningful zero.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

None — `refreshedAt=0` (empty cache) already mapped to `undefined` by upstream, so observable behavior unchanged in production. Fix makes the logic correct by domain semantics rather than relying on falsy coincidence.

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification

- Verified scenarios: 10 boundary test cases covering undefined/0/positive/mixed inputs
- Edge cases checked: zero value preservation, Math.max correctness with two positive values, nullish coalescing fallback
- What you did NOT verify: Browser rendering of usage page

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes — explicit nullish-aware merge replaces the contradictory `?? 0 || undefined` pattern with domain-correct logic
- **Refactor needed**: No
- **Alternative considered**: Keeping `?? 0 || undefined` (rejected — same bug class as #102161); extracting private `mergeRefreshedAt` function (rejected — 3-line inline expression is simpler, per AGENTS.md "Inline simple one-use objects/spreads when clearer")

## AI Assistance

- **AI model**: glm-5.1
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes

target.title: fix(signal): let controls bypass active debounce flush [AI-assisted]
target.body:
Fixes #103309

> **AI-assisted reference implementation:** this PR is intentionally written as a takeover-friendly implementation and design artifact. I understand the code path and verified the focused behavior locally; maintainers may prefer to rework or supersede it.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where authorized Signal users cannot stop or control an active agent run from the same conversation because the later control message waits behind the active Signal inbound debounce flush.

The stop/control message is delayed before OpenClaw's fast-abort, reply-admission, queue, or steering logic can inspect it. As a result, `stop` or `/stop` is often handled only after the work it was meant to interrupt has already completed.

## Why This Change Was Made

This change adds an explicit, opt-in escape hatch for urgent work in the shared keyed inbound debouncer and enables it only for authorized Signal control messages.

Ordinary same-key message ordering remains unchanged. For authorized abort requests, Signal also drops normal text that is still waiting inside the debounce window, matching the intent of Telegram's existing stop bypass and preventing stale queued work from running after the abort.

## User Impact

Signal users can issue stop/abort and other authorized control messages while a previous same-conversation agent turn is still active. The control turn reaches existing command/abort handling immediately instead of waiting for the complete prior dispatch.

Normal Signal text still batches and preserves same-key FIFO ordering. Other channels are unchanged.

## Evidence

Focused local validation on the isolated source checkout:

- `pnpm test:extension signal` — 31 files, 483 tests passed
- `CI=true pnpm vitest run src/auto-reply/inbound.test.ts src/channels/inbound-debounce-policy.test.ts` — 2 files, 65 tests passed
- `pnpm check:changed` before the final upstream rebase — core, core-test, extension, and extension-test typechecks passed; its repository-wide core lint phase exceeded the 10-minute local command limit, so the final rebased four-file TypeScript diff was checked directly with `oxlint` instead
- `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check` — passed after regenerating the checked-in API hash for the new optional parameter
- `pnpm exec oxlint <four touched TypeScript files>` — 0 warnings, 0 errors
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` for the four changed files
- `git diff --check`

No live gateway, channel monitor, Nix profile, service, or OpenClaw configuration was rebuilt, reloaded, restarted, or switched during development. The running gateway remained on its existing Nix-store build.

## Detailed technical explanation

### Failure path before this change

Signal uses a debounce key containing account, conversation, and sender. The first buffered item reserves that key immediately; when its timer fires, Signal's `onFlush` awaits `handleSignalInboundMessage()`.

That await can cover the full agent/reply operation. A later control message is correctly marked non-debounced by `shouldDebounceTextInbound()`, but `createInboundDebouncer()` still sees the active `keyChains` entry and appends the control item behind it. The message therefore cannot reach the already-existing fast-abort or queue-policy code until the prior run settles.

This is why changing `messages.queue.mode` does not repair this Signal symptom: the later turn is blocked before queue policy.

### Generic change

`InboundDebounceCreateParams<T>` gains:

```ts
shouldBypassKeyedChain?: (item: T) => boolean;
```

When the predicate returns `true`, the debouncer calls the existing guarded `runFlush()` directly rather than joining or flushing the same-key chain. The option defaults to absent, so every existing caller retains current ordering semantics. The checked-in Plugin SDK API hash is regenerated because this optional parameter is part of the exported channel-inbound debounce surface.

This is deliberately separate from `shouldDebounce=false`:

- `shouldDebounce=false` means “do not wait for a debounce timer,” but still preserves same-key ordering.
- `shouldBypassKeyedChain=true` means “this item must not wait for an active same-key operation.”

Keeping the concepts separate avoids accidentally allowing media or ordinary immediate messages to overtake conversation work.

### Signal wiring

Signal opts into the bypass only when both conditions are true:

1. the ingress authorization result marks commands as authorized; and
2. `isControlCommandMessage(entry.commandBody, cfg)` identifies an exact control command or natural-language abort trigger.

`commandBody` is used rather than the rendered/enveloped body so detection matches command processing and is not confused by quote text, sender metadata, or media placeholders.

For `isAbortRequestText(messageText)`, Signal calls `cancelKey()` on the normal conversation key before enqueueing the control entry. This only removes work still inside the debounce buffer. It does not pretend to cancel an already-running flush; the bypass lets the existing abort handler perform that job at the reply/agent layer.

### Why this is opt-in rather than a global ordering change

The generic debouncer's same-key FIFO behavior is intentional and covered by existing tests. Removing it globally could reorder ordinary channel messages, attachments, or channel-specific immediate events.

The new predicate makes the exceptional concurrency explicit at the caller that owns the control semantics. This PR wires only Signal, leaving Telegram, Feishu, and other users unchanged.

## Tests added

1. **Generic debouncer regression**
   - Starts a timer-backed same-key flush and holds it open.
   - Enqueues an opted-in non-debounced control item.
   - Asserts that the control item starts and finishes before the first flush is released.

2. **Signal active-run regression**
   - Configures a non-zero Signal inbound debounce window.
   - Holds the first Signal dispatch open.
   - Sends authorized `stop` from the same sender/conversation.
   - Asserts the second dispatch starts while the first remains blocked.

3. **Signal pending-buffer cancellation**
   - Buffers ordinary Signal work.
   - Sends an authorized natural-language abort before the timer fires.
   - Asserts only the abort reaches dispatch and the stale buffered work does not fire later.

Existing same-key ordering tests continue to cover the non-bypass default.

## Prior art and related context

- #103309 — associated bug report and full reproduction/root-cause analysis.
- #83248 / `aa71f7fe15` — Telegram's authorized stop path cancels pending debounce buffers and bypasses its normal debounce key.
- #42803 — analogous control-lane problem in Feishu.
- #48003 and #48478 — broader active-turn queue/steering reports; this patch addresses the earlier Signal ingress boundary.
- `f5ebe63ecd` — made active same-key ordering unconditional in the generic debouncer, exposing the need for an explicit control escape hatch.

## Alternatives considered

### Return a null key for Signal controls

This mirrors part of Telegram's implementation and would be smaller, but it overloads key construction with control scheduling semantics and provides less reusable intent than an explicit predicate. The proposed API documents that the caller is bypassing an active chain, not merely disabling batching.

### Change all non-debounced items to bypass active chains

Rejected because media and other immediate same-key events may rely on FIFO ordering. `shouldDebounce=false` and “may overtake active work” are not equivalent.

### Fix only reply admission / queue mode

Insufficient for this reproduction. The Signal entry does not reach reply admission while it is waiting in the channel debouncer.

### Cancel the active debounce flush

The debounce layer does not own the active agent operation and should not attempt to cancel it. It should deliver the control message promptly so the existing abort layer can cancel the correct run.

## Boundaries and non-goals

- This PR does not change ordinary Signal batching, media ordering, reply admission, queue modes, or steering semantics.
- It does not modify Telegram or Feishu behavior.
- It does not add a new user-facing command.
- It does not bypass ingress or command authorization.
- It does not attempt to cancel an already-running agent directly from the Signal extension.
- It does not edit `CHANGELOG.md`.

target.title: fix: Feishu post messages truncate URLs containing underscores
target.body:
Closes #41860

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where sending a message to Feishu containing a URL with underscores (e.g. `https://example.com/output_20260210_222435.png`) would cause the URL to be truncated or not fully clickable. Feishu's post message markdown parser interprets underscores as italics markers, breaking the URL display.

## Why This Change Was Made

A new `preserveFeishuBareMarkdownUrls()` function wraps bare URLs containing underscores in `[url](url)` markdown link syntax before sending, so Feishu's parser treats them as explicit links rather than applying italics formatting. An `` tag cannot carry a Bearer header, so the linked Personal-card 401/broken-image symptom persisted despite the RPC fix. This PR consolidates the workspace-safe avatar reader into **one shared, gateway-internal helper** (`readLocalAvatarDataUrl` in `session-utils.ts`) and uses it in **both** projections — `agent.identity.get` and the bootstrap config handler — so identity and bootstrap produce identical inline data URIs. Remote HTTP URLs, existing data URLs, text fallbacks, and the `/avatar/` HTTP endpoint are unchanged. The helper is **not** re-exported on the Plugin SDK surface (`session-utils.ts` is gateway-internal; the `identity-avatar` barrel does not re-export it). The workspace root is canonicalised with `realpathSync` to keep the containment check correct for symlinked workspaces. Fixes #97602. ## What Problem This Solves The Personal card in Control UI showed a broken avatar image because its avatar comes from the bootstrap config, not from `agent.identity.get`: - UI chat avatar → `agent.identity.get` (already fixed in the first revision). - **Config Personal card** → `appConfig.assistantIdentity.avatar` → bootstrap `control-ui-config.json` → `/avatar/` (auth-gated → `` 401). **This PR fixes this path.** Given a workspace with an avatar file `avatar.png`: - **Before**: bootstrap `assistantAvatar` = `/avatar/main` (route URL → `` 401) - **After**: bootstrap `assistantAvatar` = `data:image/png;base64,...` (inline → renders) ## Why This Change Was Made ClawSweeper's P1: the earlier fix covered only `agent.identity.get`, leaving the bootstrap Personal-card path emitting the protected route. The bootstrap config handler resolves the avatar via the same `resolveAgentAvatar(...)` and, when `kind === "local"`, inlines the file with the shared helper before `resolveAssistantAvatarUrl` (which passes data URIs through untouched). target.title: fix(msteams): add configurable timeout to Graph REST requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

MS Teams Graph REST requests (fetchGraphJson, postGraphJson, deleteGraphRequest, etc.) lacked configurable per-request timeout support. A hanging Graph API call could block the plugin indefinitely.

## Why This Change Was Made

Following the same pattern established in PR #102027 (mattermost REST client timeout), this change adds:
- Import of `resolveTimerTimeoutMs` for validated timeout values
- Configurable `timeoutMs` parameter on all Graph request functions
- Default 30-second timeout via `GRAPH_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` constant
- Caller-supplied `timeoutMs` override per request, propagated through pagination helpers

This enables callers to set tighter timeouts for specific operations (e.g., pin/unpin messages) while keeping a safe default for general requests.

## User Impact

No user-visible change with default configuration. Callers can now pass `timeoutMs` on any Graph API function to override the 30s default for specific operations.

## Evidence

- All existing msteams graph tests pass (122 tests across 10 test files)
- Pattern matches established fix(mattermost): add timeout to REST client requests (#102027)
